charts.description: Spearman rho of each 450K probe against gene expression, colored by annotation region: promoter-class probes (TSS1500/TSS200/5'UTR/1stExon) are negative (silencing), body probes positive, filled squares = p<0.05.

charts.name: The Silencing Scatter, Split by Region Class
charts.nameZh: The Silencing Scatter, Split by Region Class
charts.description: Beta value vs expression for one promoter probe (left, negative slope: methylation represses transcription) and one body probe (right, positive slope); Spearman rho annotated in each panel.

charts.name: The Reference Heatmap: Gaps Instead of Dendrograms
charts.nameZh: The Reference Heatmap: Gaps Instead of Dendrograms
charts.description: Marker average-expression heatmap for 8 cell types x CTRL/STIM: rows grouped by owning cell type (gaps between types), columns ordered CellType_CTRL | CellType_STIM with one gap between conditions; row-scaled, blue-green-red ramp.

charts.name: Reading Order Check: Row-Means by Block
charts.nameZh: Reading Order Check: Row-Means by Block
charts.description: Block means of the row-scaled heatmap (8 cell types x CTRL/STIM columns): the mean of each type's marker block is highest in its own columns, with the STIM column shifted where stimulation acts — the numeric check behind the heatmap's visual pattern.

charts.name: Essential-Gene DEG Heatmap with Patient Clustering
charts.nameZh: Essential-Gene DEG Heatmap with Patient Clustering
charts.type: CRISPR Essential Genes to TCGA DEG
charts.description: Tumour-upregulated essential genes (rows) across 118 paired samples (columns, Ward-D clustered): expression z-scored and capped at +/-2; the pT/pN strip confirms the clusters separate tumour from normal.

charts.name: The Volcano Gate: Which Essentials Are Tumour-Up?
charts.nameZh: The Volcano Gate: Which Essentials Are Tumour-Up?
charts.type: CRISPR Essential Genes to TCGA DEG
charts.description: Volcano of the paired limma test for all CERES candidates: selected tumour-upregulated essentials (padj < 0.01, log2FC > 1.5) in red; the rest grey. The planted effect sizes place the selected set cleanly in the upper-right tail.

charts.name: Nearest-Centroid Projection onto Cell Lines
charts.description: Essential-gene expression in the 24 lung-cancer cell lines, columns ordered by the nearest-centroid prediction from the TCGA-trained classifier; the annotation strip shows predicted clusters and the row dendrogram shows the gene structure.

charts.name: Drug AUC by Predicted Cluster (Kruskal–Wallis)
charts.description: Drug AUC by predicted cluster for SN-38 and talazoparib: cluster-1 (proliferative-signature) cell lines show significantly lower AUC (Kruskal-Wallis p annotated); jittered points over boxplots, one panel per drug.

charts.name: Mclust Fit and BIC Selection
charts.nameZh: Mclust 拟合与 BIC 选择
charts.description: BIC across cluster numbers (G = 1-9, VVV model family) for the 400 simulated profiles: the maximum sits at G = 5, recovering the five planted expression programmes.

charts.name: Faceted Cluster Curves with ± 1 SD Polygons
charts.nameZh: 分面簇曲线带 ± 1 SD 多边形
charts.description: Mclust cluster curves across the 12 embryo time points: cluster mean (line) with +/- 1 SD polygon, one facet per cluster with the gene count printed. The five planted programmes (maternal decay, zygotic rise, mid-peak, constant high/low) are each recovered as a cluster.

charts.name: The Screen: 2000+ Pairwise Log-Rank Tests
charts.description: Bonferroni-adjusted log-rank p (log10, capped) for all surviving gene pairs: the planted IL7R-vs-GZMB ordering is the single genome-wide-significant pair; the null family spreads over 3-6 orders of magnitude of adjusted p.

charts.name: The Winning Pair's Kaplan–Meier
charts.description: Kaplan-Meier of the top-ranked pair (IL7R vs GZMB, Bonferroni p < 0.05): score 1 (IL7R < GZMB, cytotoxic dominance) carries the survival advantage; the reference's IRGPI index is built by extending this same log-rank + lasso step over several pairs.

charts.name: Regulon Activity Across Subtypes
charts.nameZh: 跨亚型的 regulon 活性
charts.description: Regulon activity profiles for 23 urothelial TF regulons across 120 samples in four subtypes: columns grouped by subtype (gap-separated, sample names omitted), rows z-scaled and capped at +/-2.5; each subtype's planted programme (e.g. TP63/KLF4 in iBS1, PPARG/RXRA in iLS3) lights up as a red block.

charts.name: Subtype-Mean Activity: The Condensed Readout
charts.nameZh: 亚型均值活性：浓缩读法
charts.description: Mean +/- SD regulon activity per subtype for the ten TFs with the largest between-subtype spread: each planted programme separates its own subtype clearly, housekeeping regulons stay near zero everywhere.

charts.name: KM Curves with the Two RMST Horizons
charts.nameZh: 带两个 RMST 地平线的 KM 曲线
charts.description: Overall survival by subtype to 12 months with dashed horizons at the two RMST cut-offs (6/12 months): the resistant CS2 separates early, CS3/CS4 show the delayed immunotherapy pattern.

charts.name: Pairwise RMST p-Value Matrices (6 and 12 Months)
charts.nameZh: 逐对 RMST p 值矩阵（6 与 12 个月）
charts.description: Pairwise RMST-difference p values at tau = 180 days (lower triangle of each block) and tau = 365 (upper): CS2 is significant against CS1/CS3 at both horizons, while the delayed CS3-vs-CS1 pair only separates at 12 months.

charts.name: The Delayed-Effect Landmark Test
charts.nameZh: 延迟效应的 landmark 检验
charts.description: Landmark log-rank at t0 = 90 days (patients alive at 90 days, residual survival): the delayed CS3 arm separates from the resistant CS2 only after the landmark, which the unconditioned overall log-rank would dilute.

charts.name: The Prediction: Ridge Models per Drug
charts.description: Ridge prediction of tumour IC50: per-drug models trained on cell lines (top, training-set observed vs fitted) transfer to tumours (bottom, predicted IC50 distribution by immune cluster). SN-38 and Gemcitabine separate C1/C2; the rest stay flat.

charts.name: Wilcoxon Screen and Boxplots of the Significant Drugs
charts.nameZh: Wilcoxon 筛选与显著药物箱线图
charts.description: Predicted IC50 by immune cluster for the four lowest-Wilcoxon-p drugs: SN-38 and Gemcitabine (planted mechanism) show significant C1 vs C2 differences; the flat drugs stay non-significant. p from Wilcoxon rank-sum, annotated per panel.

charts.name: The SNF Core and the Fused Network
charts.description: The SNF-fused similarity network for the same 90 patients (columns and rows ordered by the fused clustering): the two planted blocks read as sharp diagonal squares — visibly cleaner than either single view in the next figure.

charts.name: The SNF Core and the Fused Network
charts.description: The two single-view similarity matrices in the same fused-cluster order: both carry the two-block structure, but with view-specific noise that the fusion smooths away.

charts.name: Fused-Cluster Agreement with the Planted Subtypes
charts.nameZh: 融合簇与植入亚型的一致性
charts.description: Methylation (left) and expression (right) z-scored views, columns ordered by SNF cluster with the planted-subtype annotation strip: both views align with the fused labels (adjusted Rand index in the caption), the multi-omics claim of the method.

charts.name: Arm-Level Amplification and Deletion Frequencies
charts.description: Arm-level CNV frequencies by immune-score group: amplification (left) and deletion (right) percentages per chromosome arm, Im-H vs Im-L; Fisher-tested arms (planted 7q/8q/20q amplification and 9p/13q deletion excess in Im-L) are marked with their p values.

charts.name: Focal-Level Amplification and Deletion Levels
charts.nameZh: 焦点级扩增与缺失水平
charts.description: Focal-level amplification (left) and deletion (right) levels per patient by group: Im-L melanomas carry significantly higher focal burden (Wilcoxon p annotated), consistent with the arm-level excess.

charts.name: Chromosome Ideogram with Gene Labels
charts.nameZh: 染色体 ideogram 与基因标签
charts.description: Circular gene-location layout: 23 chromosomes drawn as a shaded ideogram ring (10-Mb bins), the 14 candidate genes marked at their positions with labelled markers, ordered by chromosome; the CNV-class colour ring appears in the next figure.

charts.name: CNV-Class Track Under the Ideogram
charts.nameZh: ideogram 下的 CNV 类别轨道
charts.description: Gene locations with CNV-class track: ideogram ring + gene markers as before, plus an inner ring where each gene's CNV class is colour-coded (red = amplified, grey = neutral, blue = deleted).

charts.name: Stacked Gain/Loss/Neutral Frequencies
charts.description: Per-gene CNV class frequencies across 380 simulated tumours: gain (red) stacked over loss (blue) with copy-neutral (green) completing each column; genes ordered by total alteration frequency, the recurrent-gain writers leading.

charts.name: Gain-Biased Genes Highlighted
charts.nameZh: 高亮 gain 偏向基因
charts.description: Gain vs loss frequency per gene: the six planted recurrent-gain genes sit far above the balance diagonal, the four recurrent-loss genes far below; neutral-heavy genes cluster at the origin. Labels on the extremes.

charts.name: The Stacked Three-Family Overview
charts.description: TIME overview across 120 samples sorted by MeTIL score: MeTIL strip (top), CIBERSORT 16 cell-type block (middle), MCP-counter 2 stromal scores (bottom) — the immune-hot/cold gradient runs left to right through all three panels.

charts.name: Per-Family Subtype Contrast
charts.description: Mean z-scored CIBERSORT fraction per subtype: cytotoxic T cells, activated NK and DCs are high in the hot subtypes (CS1/CS3), naive B cells and neutrophils in the cold CS2 — the contrast the overview heatmap visualizes.

charts.name: Spearman ρ per Regulator (Gated Cohort)
charts.nameZh: 门控队列的逐调控子 Spearman ρ
charts.description: Spearman rho between each epigenetic regulator and the CTL score in the 117 (simulated: 117) high-CD8-infiltration melanoma samples: bars filled by significance (red = p < 0.05, grey = ns); the planted FTO-positive and METTL3/CBX4-negative associations dominate.

charts.name: The Anchor Scatter: FTO vs CTL Score
charts.nameZh: 锚定散点：FTO vs CTL 评分
charts.description: FTO expression vs CTL score (mean of CD8A, CD8B, GZMA, GZMB, PRF1) in the high-infiltration subset: linear trend with the Spearman rho annotated — the positive association that motivates the pan-regulator screen.

charts.name: The Dot Grid: rho × Significance per Gene × Cancer
charts.nameZh: 点网格：逐基因 × 癌种的 rho × 显著性
charts.description: Spearman correlation between CNA and expression, per gene (rows) x cancer (columns): dot size = -log10(p) (capped at 12), colour = direction (red = positive, blue = negative). The planted cis-effects (SLC7A11, GPX4 positive; MT1G negative in KIRC) stand out from the null family.

charts.name: The Companion Heatmap: Signed −log10(p)
charts.description: Signed -log10(p) heatmap (positive = red, negative = blue) with per-gene counts of significant cancers as the row annotation: the SLC7A11/GPX4 rows are significant in nearly every type; MT1G's single significant point is the KIRC negative.

charts.name: Gain/Loss Frequencies per Cancer
charts.description: Fraction of tumours with a copy-number gain (red) or loss (blue) of any ferroptosis-panel gene, per cancer type: the planted hot types (LIHC, BLCA, HNSC) lead the gain axis; KIRC leads the loss axis.

charts.name: Per-Gene Resolution Inside the Hot Type
charts.nameZh: 热门类型内的逐基因分辨率
charts.description: Per-gene gain frequency within the hottest cancer (LIHC): the six planted high-frequency genes (SLC7A11, GPX4, NFE2L2 and companions) dominate, with genes colour-coded by whether they exceed the cohort median.

charts.name: Significant-DEG Counts per Cancer
charts.nameZh: 逐癌种显著 DEG 计数
charts.description: Number of significant tumour-vs-normal DE genes per cancer type (limma, FDR < 0.05): up-regulated in red, down-regulated in green; the planted hot types (KIRC, LUAD, HNSC) carry the largest bars.

charts.name: Fold-Change Heatmap with Significance Marks
charts.nameZh: 倍数变化热图 + 显著性格线
charts.description: log2 fold change (tumour vs normal) per cancer x gene, drawn as white-bodied cells with coloured outlines: red = significant up, green = significant down, grey = FDR >= 0.05; the planted programmes (SLC7A11/GPX4/NFE2L2 up, MT1G/ALOX15 down) read as coloured rows.

charts.name: Median Pathway Score per Cell Type
charts.nameZh: 逐细胞类型的通路中位评分
charts.description: Median metabolic pathway score per cell type (rank-based, 0-1): MRC1+ macrophages peak on glycolysis and fatty-acid oxidation, CD8/NK cells on OXPHOS — the planted programme structure.

charts.name: Average Expression of the Druggable Genes
charts.nameZh: 可成药基因的平均表达
charts.description: Average expression of the fatty-acid-oxidation pathway's druggable genes per cell type (top 10 by MRC1+ macrophage expression): the macrophage column leads, anchoring the pathway-score block of the previous heatmap to named targets.

charts.name: Consensus Cluster Heatmap
charts.description: Consensus co-clustering frequency matrix (100 resamples) with the discovered class labels: three near-perfect blocks confirm the sample classes are stable under resampling.

charts.name: Leave-One-Out Classifier Accuracy
charts.description: Leave-one-out accuracy of five classifiers trained on the discovered classes: nearest centroid and LDA reach ~95-100%, 3NN and SVM slightly lower, 1NN most sensitive to single-sample noise.

charts.name: Heatmap with Overlaid Asterisk Dots
charts.description: Gene expression heatmap (12 genes × 10 patients) with white asterisk dots overlaid on statistically significant cells (p < 0.05): clean color grid without text clutter.

charts.name: P-Value Gradients as Dot Size
charts.nameZh: 以点大小编码 p 值的替代方案
charts.description: Alternative encoding: dot size proportional to -log10(p) overlaid on heatmap tiles, combining effect size (color) and confidence (dot size) in one view.

charts.name: Cancer × Pathway Correlation Heatmap
charts.nameZh: 癌种 × 通路相关热图
charts.description: Correlation between the per-sample NETs-style score and 10 malignant-feature pathways across 12 cancer types: the six planted pathways show consistent positive rho (red) with significance stars, while the four independent pathways stay near zero.

charts.name: One Cancer in Detail: Scatter and Effect Ranking
charts.nameZh: 单癌种细节：散点与效应排序
charts.description: LUAD detail: left, the score vs proliferation scatter with fitted trend (rho annotated); right, all ten pathways ranked by rho, showing the six linked pathways clustered at the top and the four independent ones near zero.

charts.name: Ro/e Line Profiles, All Clusters
charts.nameZh: 全部簇的 Ro/e 折线剖面
charts.description: Tissue-enrichment line profiles: Ro/e of each cluster plotted across the four regions (core to distal), with the Ro/e = 1 null line; myeloid/mast clusters peak in the core and decline outward, lymphoid clusters do the opposite.

charts.name: Region Totals as the Denominator
charts.description: Cells per region (the denominator behind every Ro/e point): the distal region carries the fewest cells, so its Ro/e values are the least stable — the caveat the ratio panel cannot show.

charts.name: Circular Bar Chart (Wheel Chart)
charts.description: Circular proportional wheel chart representing 30 compositional categories grouped into 4 domains: wedge height encodes percentage proportion, coloured by domain.

charts.name: The Circos Link Plot
charts.description: Circular connectivity layout for 28 brain regions across 7 functional networks: outer sectors coloured by network, inner ribbons show the top 5% strongest functional connections (red = positive, blue = negative).

charts.name: Grouped Chord Diagram Alternative
charts.description: Inter-network chord diagram summarizing connection counts between the seven functional networks: chord thickness encodes connection volume, colours match the network palette.

charts.name: Ro/e Dot Heatmap
charts.description: Tissue preference by Ro/e: clusters (rows) x tissues (columns), tile colour shows enrichment (red, Ro/e > 1) or depletion (blue, Ro/e < 1) with the Ro/e value printed and the dot size proportional to cell number; mast and myeloid clusters prefer the plaque core, lymphocytes the lymph node.

charts.name: The Chi-Square Residual Check
charts.description: Pearson residuals of the same cluster x tissue table (chi-square test): the planted core-preferring and lymph-node-preferring blocks show large positive residuals, confirming the Ro/e pattern is statistically supported rather than driven by small counts.

charts.name: The Genome-Ordered CNV Heatmap
charts.nameZh: 基因组排序的 CNV 热图
charts.description: Genome-wide CNV heatmap (1200 genes in chromosome order x 120 tumours): red = gain, blue = loss; the planted chr3 gain in GC1 and chr9 loss in GC2 read as broad stripes, the chr8 focal amplification as a narrow hot streak shared by all classes.

charts.name: Per-Class CNV Burden
charts.description: Per-class CNV burden: fraction of gene-sample calls that are gains (left) and losses (right); GC1 carries the highest gain burden, GC2 the highest loss burden, quantitating the two planted arm-level events.

charts.name: Stacked Proportion Barplot of Clinical Stage by Subtype
charts.nameZh: 亚型临床分期堆叠比例条形图
charts.description: Distribution of clinical stages across three HCC molecular subtypes (S1-S3): 100% stacked barplot showing that subtype S1 is enriched for advanced stage (Stage III/IV) patients (Chi-square test p < 0.01).

charts.name: Immunomodulator Expression Heatmap across Subtypes
charts.nameZh: 亚型间免疫调节剂表达热图
charts.description: Expression of 24 immunomodulator genes across 152 tumour samples grouped by immune subtype (C1-C4): rows z-scaled and capped at +/-2.5; co-inhibitory checkpoints and chemokines show pronounced up-regulation in hot subtypes (C1/C3).

charts.name: Checkpoint Expression by Subtype (Boxplot Summary)
charts.nameZh: 按亚型的检验点表达（箱线图汇总）
charts.description: Mean expression of key immune checkpoints (PD-1, CTLA-4, LAG-3, TIGIT) across immune subtypes: hot subtypes (C1/C3) exhibit significantly higher checkpoint expression than cold subtypes (C2/C4).

charts.name: Imputation Restores the Co-Expression Axis
charts.type: MAGIC Imputation and knnDREMI Gene Modules
charts.description: MAGIC-style kNN diffusion imputation: raw expression of a strongly co-varying gene vs PLCG2 is a dropout cloud (left), while the 3-round diffusion imputation restores the linear co-expression axis (right).

charts.name: knnDREMI Scores and the Module Heatmap
charts.type: MAGIC Imputation and knnDREMI Gene Modules
charts.description: knnDREMI screening and module heatmap: left, the DREMI score distribution with the >1 threshold marked (the 30 planted co-varying genes form the high tail); right, z-scored imputed expression of the top 30 genes ordered by PLCG2 with hierarchical module assignment, reproducing the three planted modules.

charts.name: Pseudotime Gradient and Branch States on UMAP
charts.nameZh: UMAP 上的拟时序梯度与分支状态
charts.description: Single-cell pseudotime trajectory (Monocle-style) on UMAP embedding: cells coloured by pseudotime progression (left, viridis gradient) and by developmental branch state (right, 3 states).

charts.name: Stacked Proportion Barplot per Patient
charts.nameZh: 逐病人的堆叠比例条形图
charts.description: Estimated cell-type proportions per bulk RNA-seq sample (MuSiC deconvolution): stacked 100% barplot grouped by 4 clinical groups (G1-G4); T cells and Monocytes dominate across all patients, with visible group-level shifts.

charts.name: Group-Level Cell-Type Abundance Boxplots
charts.nameZh: 组级细胞类型丰度箱线图
charts.description: Cell-type proportion distributions across the four clinical groups: T cells show a significant group-level difference (Wilcoxon p annotated), validating the visual shift from the stacked bar.

charts.name: Pairwise Odds Ratio Heatmap
charts.type: Somatic Mutation Mutual Exclusivity and Co-Occurrence
charts.description: Pairwise somatic mutation interaction heatmap (odds ratio): blue squares indicate mutual exclusivity (e.g. GENE01 vs GENE02), red squares indicate co-occurrence; significant pairs (Fisher exact test p < 0.05) marked with asterisks.

charts.name: Frequency Barplot of Individual Gene Mutations
charts.nameZh: 单个基因突变频率条形图
charts.type: Somatic Mutation Mutual Exclusivity and Co-Occurrence
charts.description: Individual gene mutation frequencies (%) across the 200 tumour samples: GENE01 and GENE02 lead the cohort frequency.

charts.name: PAM Shrunken Centroids
charts.description: PAM shrunken centroids (3 subtypes x top marker genes): after soft-threshold shrinkage only the subtype-specific markers retain signal, giving each subtype a compact template.

charts.name: NTP Prediction on the Independent Cohort
charts.nameZh: 独立队列上的 NTP 预测
charts.description: NTP prediction on an independent cohort with a simulated platform shift (offset + extra noise): the confusion matrix shows near-complete recovery of the three subtypes, and the per-sample best-template correlation is clearly separated from the permutation null.

charts.name: Three-Track Circular Score Map
charts.description: Pan-cancer circular score map: from outside in, the tissue system ring, the cancer-type ring, and the mean senescence-style score bar track; cancers are ordered by tissue so each system occupies one arc.

charts.name: Tissue-Level Aggregation
charts.description: Mean score per tissue system with individual cancer values overlaid as points: Reproductive and Skin lead, Haematologic is lowest, matching the arc pattern of the circular map.

charts.name: Expression vs Methylation Correlation Grid
charts.nameZh: 表达 vs 甲基化相关网格
charts.description: Spearman correlation between gene expression and promoter methylation per gene (rows) x cancer (columns): dot size = -log10(p) (capped at 12), colour = direction (blue = negative silencing, red = positive). SLC7A11 and GPX4 show consistent promoter silencing across almost all tumour types.

charts.name: Representative Scatter: SLC7A11 in BRCA
charts.nameZh: 代表性散点：BRCA 中的 SLC7A11
charts.description: Promoter methylation beta value vs gene expression for SLC7A11 in BRCA (n = 300): negative Spearman correlation (rho = -0.72, p < 1e-15) reflecting epigenetic silencing of transcription.

charts.name: Tumour vs Normal Methylation per Cancer Type
charts.nameZh: 逐癌种肿瘤 vs 正常甲基化
charts.description: Promoter DNA methylation beta values (tumour vs normal) across 12 cancer types for the ferroptosis gene panel: tumour tissues show significant hypomethylation (Wilcoxon p annotated) in planted hot types (LIHC, KIRC, LUAD, COAD), consistent with transcriptional activation.

charts.name: Per-Gene Methylation in the Hottest Cancer Type
charts.nameZh: 最热癌种内的逐基因甲基化
charts.description: Per-gene promoter methylation beta values in LIHC (tumour vs normal): SLC7A11 and GPX4 show the pronounced tumour hypomethylation that permits their pan-cancer overexpression.

charts.name: Mutation Frequency Bar Chart
charts.description: Somatic mutation frequency (%) of pathway regulators across 120 samples: the top recurrently mutated genes exceed 30% frequency, while tail genes show low mutation rates.

charts.name: Mutation Oncoplot (Variant Types)
charts.description: Somatic mutation oncoplot showing variant distribution across 120 samples (columns) and pathway genes (rows): colours encode variant class (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift_Del, Splice_Site, Multi_Hit).

charts.name: UMAP Embedding Highlighted by AUCell Score
charts.nameZh: AUCell 评分高亮的 UMAP 嵌入
charts.description: UMAP visualization of 1500 single cells coloured by ISG AUCell signature score (left) and binary thresholded high-score cells (right, threshold = 85th percentile): Monocytes and pDCs light up as the ISG-high populations.

charts.name: Distribution Across Cell Clusters (Violin Plot)
charts.nameZh: 跨细胞簇的分布（小提琴图）
charts.description: AUCell signature score distribution across single-cell clusters (violin plot with jittered points): Monocytes and pDCs show significantly elevated ISG activity compared to T, B, and NK cells.

charts.name: Static Igraph Correlation Network
charts.nameZh: 静态 Igraph 关联网络
charts.type: Correlation Network of Bulk & Single-Cell Signatures
charts.description: Correlative cell-cell interaction network from bulk abundance estimates (Spearman rho > 0.45): nodes coloured by global cluster (Paired palette), edges representing co-abundance across 308 colorectal cancer samples.

charts.name: Adjacency Heatmap of Correlated Cell Types
charts.nameZh: 相关细胞类型的邻接热图
charts.type: Correlation Network of Bulk & Single-Cell Signatures
charts.description: Thresholded abundance correlation matrix (rho > 0.45): the myeloid-stromal module and lymphoid module appear as distinct positive blocks, confirming the network edges.

charts.name: The Two-Colour Merge Map
charts.description: Single-cell co-expression merge map: gene A alone (red), gene B alone (green), and the merged view where double-positive cells blend to yellow — only a minority of fibroblasts co-express both markers.

charts.name: Co-Expression Matrix and Correlation
charts.description: Co-expression summary: left, the 2x2 high/low matrix counts showing most cells are single-positive; right, the Pearson correlation of A vs B among marker-positive fibroblasts with its strength class annotated.

charts.name: Per-Sample Fraction by Cancer Type
charts.description: Fraction of LAMP3+ cDCs derived from the cDC2 subset, per tumour sample, across six cancer types: cDC2-derived cells dominate in most cancers while LUAD carries a distinctly lower fraction (Kruskal-Wallis p annotated); point size encodes the number of LAMP3+ cDCs in that sample.

charts.name: Pooled Composition Per Cancer Type
charts.description: Pooled origin composition of LAMP3+ cDCs per cancer type (100% stacked): cDC2-derived dominates everywhere, with LUAD's larger cDC1-derived share visible; pooled bars are shown alongside the per-sample spread in the previous panel, not as a replacement for it.

charts.name: Per-Cell Score Scatter With Assignment
charts.nameZh: 逐细胞评分散点与分配
charts.description: Signature-score stratification of 900 dendritic cells: cells are placed by their cDC1 vs cDC2 signature score and coloured by the argmax assignment, so the three subsets separate into three regions and the planted mislabeled cells fall into the wrong region.

charts.name: Agreement Between Cluster and Score Assignment
charts.nameZh: 簇与评分分配的一致性
charts.description: Agreement between the original clusters and the score-based assignment: the diagonal dominates, and the off-diagonal cells are the planted mislabeled minority; the right panel shows the mean score profile per cluster, the evidence behind the assignment.

charts.name: The Trajectory With Lineages
charts.type: Slingshot Lineage Trajectory and Gene Dynamics
charts.description: Slingshot-style lineage inference on a branching single-cell embedding: eight clusters (left to right of the root) with two principal-curve lineages, effector (upper) and memory (lower), drawn over the cells.

charts.name: Gene Dynamics Along Each Lineage
charts.type: Slingshot Lineage Trajectory and Gene Dynamics
charts.description: Marker gene dynamics along pseudotime by lineage: the effector lineage rises steeply past the branch point while the memory lineage stays low — the lineage-specific programme the trajectory was built to reveal.

charts.name: Kaplan–Meier Survival Curve by TIL Group
charts.nameZh: TIL 组 Kaplan–Meier 生存曲线
charts.description: Kaplan-Meier overall survival curves stratified by TIL signature score (High vs Low): patients with high tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte scores show significantly better survival (log-rank p < 0.01).

charts.name: TME Feature Boxplots Across Subtypes
charts.nameZh: 跨亚型的 TME 特征箱线图
charts.description: Faceted boxplots of four TME infiltration features (Stromal score, Immune score, Macrophage fraction, CD8+ T cells) across 150 soft-tissue sarcoma samples grouped by histological subtype; Kruskal-Wallis p values annotated.

charts.name: Correlation Heatmap of TME Features
charts.description: Spearman correlation heatmap of TME features across all STS samples: stromal and macrophage scores correlate positively, while CD8 T cells form an orthogonal axis.

charts.name: Regulon Activity Scores (VIPER-Style z)
charts.nameZh: Regulon 活性评分（VIPER 式 z）
charts.description: Regulon activity z-scores (VIPER-style rank enrichment) for 12 TFs across 60 tumour and 60 normal samples: the four planted activators (STAT3, MYC, NFKB1, HIF1A) show a clear tumour-high block, the three repressed TFs a tumour-low block.

charts.name: The Differential-Activity Ranking
charts.description: Differential regulon activity (tumour minus normal) per TF with BH-adjusted p values: the four planted activators rank positive and significant, the three repressors negative and significant, the remaining five near zero.

charts.name: Observed and Predicted ASIR Trends by Country
charts.nameZh: 国家观察值与预测值 ASIR 趋势
charts.description: Trends in observed (solid lines, 1985-2020) and BAPC-predicted (dashed lines, 2025-2030) age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR per 100,000) with 95% confidence intervals across four countries: all countries show a projected downward trajectory.

charts.name: Age-Specific Rates Across Time Periods
charts.nameZh: 跨时期的年龄特异速率
charts.description: Age-specific incidence rates across the 8 time periods (1985-2020) for one representative country (Japan): rates peak in older age groups (70-79, 80+) and decline over time across all age brackets.

charts.name: Expression vs ORR Scatter Plot
charts.nameZh: 表达 vs ORR 散点图
charts.description: Scatter plot of gene expression vs Objective Response Rate (ORR %) across 80 clinical samples: positive correlation (Spearman rho = 0.78, p < 1e-15) indicating higher expression associates with better treatment response.

charts.name: Drug Sensitivity AUC Boxplots Across Subtypes
charts.nameZh: 亚型间药物敏感性 AUC 箱线图
charts.description: Predicted drug response AUCs for Sorafenib and Lenvatinib across three HCC molecular subtypes (S1-S3): subtype S2 exhibits significantly lower Sorafenib AUC (higher sensitivity), while S1 is more sensitive to Lenvatinib (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001).

charts.name: Risk-Stratified Kaplan–Meier Survival Curve
charts.nameZh: 风险分层 Kaplan–Meier 生存曲线
charts.description: Kaplan-Meier overall survival curves stratified by prognostic signature risk score (High vs Low risk): high-risk patients show significantly poorer survival (log-rank p < 0.001).

charts.name: Time-Dependent AUC Barplot
charts.nameZh: 时间依赖性 AUC 条形图
charts.description: Time-dependent AUC values for the prognostic signature at 1, 3, and 5 years: AUC remains above 0.70 across all three follow-up intervals, indicating robust predictive performance.

charts.name: The Four-Endpoint Prognostic Heatmap
charts.description: Prognostic heatmap of one gene across 14 cancers x 4 survival endpoints: red = risk factor (HR > 1, p < 0.05), green = protective (HR < 1, p < 0.05), white = non-significant; colour intensity scales with -log10(p).

charts.name: The Hazard-Ratio Forest Summary
charts.description: OS hazard ratios per cancer with 95% confidence intervals: cancers in the planted risk class sit right of the null line with red markers, the protective class left with green.

charts.name: The Weighted Score Distribution
charts.description: Distribution of the weighted pathway-mutation score (PMAP) across 180 patients, sorted: most patients carry few mutations so the score is right-skewed; the median splits low from high.

charts.name: Kaplan–Meier by Score Group
charts.description: Kaplan-Meier overall survival by PMAP group (median split): the high-score group shows significantly worse survival (log-rank p annotated), confirming the weighted adverse genes drive the separation.

charts.name: Required Events vs Hazard Ratio
charts.nameZh: 所需事件数 vs 风险比
charts.description: Required number of events (Schoenfeld's approximation) vs hazard ratio at 80% and 90% power: a HR of 0.7 needs ~247 events at 80% power, while a HR of 0.5 needs only ~65.

charts.name: Required Patients Given Expected Event Rate
charts.nameZh: 给定事件率下的所需患者数
charts.description: Required number of patients (events / expected event rate) for three event rates across the same HR range: lower event rates dramatically inflate the required cohort size.

charts.name: Circular Contribution Barplot
charts.description: Disease contribution scores for 8 macrophage subsets as a circular barplot: bar length encodes the normalised score (differential abundance x expression magnitude), coloured by rank; Mac_01 has the highest contribution.

charts.name: Component Breakdown: Abundance vs Expression
charts.nameZh: 成分拆解：丰度 vs 表达
charts.description: Differential abundance (log2 fold-change of cell fraction) vs differential expression magnitude for each subset: Mac_01 is high on both axes; Mac_02's rank is driven by expression while its abundance barely changes; Mac_06-Mac_08 shift strongly in abundance (down) but have low expression magnitude, placing them mid-rank.

charts.name: Shared Clonotype Heatmap
charts.type: Shared Clonotype Heatmap Across Cell Types
charts.description: Shared clonotype heatmap between 6 T-cell phenotypic clusters: colour = log10(number of shared clonotypes) on a white-to-red scale; the Terminal-exhausted/Effector-memory pair carries the largest overlap (heterogeneous clonotypes), while Naive clonotypes are mostly homogeneous.

charts.name: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Clonotype Classification
charts.nameZh: 同质 vs 异质克隆型分类
charts.type: Shared Clonotype Heatmap Across Cell Types
charts.description: Relative numbers of homogeneous (grey) vs heterogeneous (coloured) clonotypes per cluster: Naive carries mostly homogeneous clonotypes, while Terminally exhausted and Effector memory carry a larger heterogeneous share.

charts.name: SSEA Radar Chart
charts.description: SSEA radar chart: 8 metabolic pathways as spokes, three molecular subtypes as coloured polygons, scores globally scaled to [0, 1]; S1 peaks on Glycolysis (second: Pentose phosphate), S2 on OXPHOS and Fatty-acid oxidation, S3 on Glutamine metabolism and TCA cycle.

charts.name: Heatmap Companion: Raw SSE Scores
charts.nameZh: 热图补充：原始 SSE 分数
charts.description: Raw mean GSVA enrichment scores per subtype x pathway (the unnormalised companion to the radar): S1 is Glycolysis-high, S2 is OXPHOS/Fatty-acid-high, S3 is Glutamine/TCA-high; printed numbers give exact values.

charts.name: Spatial Scatter of Total Microbial UMIs
charts.nameZh: 微生物 UMI 总数的空间散点
charts.description: Spatial distribution of total microbial UMIs across the Visium spot grid: tumour-nest regions (high E. coli abundance) show elevated microbial counts compared to stroma and normal epithelium.

charts.name: Region-Specific Microbial Species Breakdown
charts.nameZh: 区域特异的微生物物种分解
charts.description: Median microbial UMI per species per histological region: E. coli is enriched in tumour nests, B. fragilis in stroma, and both are near-zero in normal epithelium - the region-specific pattern the spatial scatter visualises.

charts.name: Adonis R2 Barplot of Significant Host Factors
charts.nameZh: 显著宿主因子的 Adonis R2 条形图
charts.description: PERMANOVA (Bray-Curtis, 999 permutations) contributions of host factors to community variation: bars are the per-term R2 of factors significant after BH correction (FDR < 0.05), sorted by R2 and coloured by metadata category; Disease and both medications dominate, mirroring the planted effects.

charts.name: Permutation p-values vs Effect Size
charts.nameZh: 置换 p 值 vs 效应量
charts.description: Per-factor effect size (R2) vs permutation p-value (log scale): filled circles pass BH correction at 5%; Disease/Medication_A/Medication_B are large and highly significant, while BMI and Age sit near the borderline and socioeconomic factors explain almost no variance.

charts.name: Pathway t-Value Barplot (Tumour vs Normal)
charts.nameZh: 通路 t 值条形图（肿瘤 vs 正常）
charts.description: limma t-statistics of GSVA pathway scores, tumour versus normal (BH-adjusted significant pathways only): epithelial-mesenchymal transition, hypoxia and glycolysis are tumour-up (red), interferon-alpha/gamma responses and inflammatory response are normal-up (green); each bar carries its pathway label at the tip.

charts.name: GSVA Score Heatmap of Significant Pathways
charts.nameZh: 显著通路的 GSVA 分数热图
charts.description: GSVA scores (rows z-scored) for the significant pathways across all 20 samples: tumour samples carry high EMT/hypoxia/glycolysis and low interferon-response scores, normal samples the inverse; column annotations mark the group.

charts.name: Infiltration Heatmap Ordered by CD274 Expression
charts.nameZh: 按 CD274 表达排序的浸润热图
charts.description: MCP-counter style infiltration heatmap for 120 LGG samples (rows z-scored, spearman clustering): columns ordered by ascending CD274 (PD-L1) expression; the CD8 T-cell/cytotoxic block increases along the PD-L1 axis (adaptive immune resistance) and IDH-wildtype samples carry higher monocyte/macrophage scores.

charts.name: Population Scores Against the PD-L1 Axis
charts.nameZh: 各群体评分沿 PD-L1 轴的变化
charts.description: Mean infiltration score per population across CD274-expression quartiles: CD8 T cells and cytotoxic lymphocytes rise monotonically with PD-L1 (immune-resistance axis), monocytes/macrophages stay IDH-driven, and B cells show no trend.

charts.name: CD8 Subclusters Mapped onto the Trajectory (FigureYa40lineage)
charts.nameZh: CD8 亚群映射到轨迹上（FigureYa40lineage）
charts.description: CD8 T-cell subclusters on the same trajectory (left): LEF1+ (naive) at the root, CX3CR1+ (memory) at early pseudotime, and GZMK+/LAYN+ (effector/exhausted) occupying the two terminal branches; right, cluster composition per branch state — each late state is dominated by one effector subcluster.

charts.name: TMB Boxplot with Wilkinson Dotplot
charts.nameZh: TMB 箱线图与 Wilkinson 点图
charts.type: Tumor Mutation Burden by Expression Group
charts.description: Tumour mutational burden (non-silent mutations per Mb) by gene-expression group (median split): high expressers carry a significantly higher TMB (Wilcoxon p < 0.001), the planted mutator effect; each dot is one patient.

charts.name: Overall Survival by TMB Group
charts.nameZh: 按 TMB 分组的总生存
charts.type: Tumor Mutation Burden by Expression Group
charts.description: Overall survival by TMB group (median split): the high-TMB arm shows better survival (log-rank p < 0.0001), consistent with higher neoantigen load; shaded bands are the 95% confidence intervals.

charts.name: Cophenetic Coefficient for Method Choice
charts.nameZh: 方法选择的共表型系数
charts.description: NMF cophenetic correlation across ranks 2-6 (20 runs per rank): the coefficient peaks at rank 3, the planted subtype number, and falls as ranks fragment the structure — the classical consensus-clustering model-choice criterion.

charts.name: Hierarchical Consensus Matrix
charts.description: Hierarchical consensus matrix at k = 3 (40 runs at 80% subsampling), samples ordered by consensus subtype: three dark diagonal blocks with near-zero off-block co-clustering — the subtype structure is stable under resampling.

charts.name: Method-to-Method Agreement
charts.description: Method-to-method agreement at k = 3 (rows and columns are cluster labels 1-3): CC, CNMF and SNF pairs are all diagonal-dominant — the three algorithms recover the same three subtypes, evidence the structure is data-driven.

charts.name: Survival by Consensus Subtype
charts.description: Overall survival by SNF consensus subtype: the poor-prognosis subtype (3) separates from the other two (log-rank p < 0.001) — the clinical relevance read-out the reference pairs with the clustering comparison.

charts.name: Multi-omics Circos Ring
charts.nameZh: 多组学 Circos 环形图
charts.description: Multi-omics circos across 8 chromosomes (Mb scale): arcs coloured by copy-number state (red Gain / blue Loss) with gene-level expression log2FC scattered on the inner ring; the chr7q Gain and chr12p Loss line up with the co-directed gene scatter, the planted multi-omics concordance.

charts.name: chr7 Zoom with Gene Labels
charts.description: chr7 zoom: the q-arm Gain arcs (red) carry the up-scattered genes; only the strongest-effect genes are labelled, so no two names collide.

charts.name: Group Conservation Profiles
charts.description: Mean phastCons conservation across the 2 kb window for normal (green) and tumour (red) samples: the two ancestral conserved peaks (~300 and ~1650) persist in both groups, while the element at ~975 drops from 0.80 to ~0.35 in tumour — the group-specific disruption the overlay is built to expose.

charts.name: Per-Element Mean Score Comparison
charts.description: Per-sample mean phastCons inside the three elements: shared elements (left, right) overlap between normal and tumour, while the tumour-specific element (~975) separates cleanly (Wilcoxon p < 0.001) — the numerical support for the profile overlay.

charts.name: Yearly Publication Trend
charts.description: Annual count of CD274/PD-L1 articles in the simulated corpus (2015-2024): the curve rises steeply through the immunotherapy era, the module-1 growth trend the reference extracts from a PubMed year filter.

charts.name: Gene "Friends" from Abstract Word Frequencies
charts.nameZh: 摘要词频里的"基因好友"
charts.description: Gene word frequencies across the 300 CD274 abstracts (module 3, target gene excluded): the planted immune-escape axis dominates — PDCD1/PD-1, CD8A, GZMB, LAG3 and TIGIT are the 'gene friends' a reader would follow up, while distant-pathway genes appear rarely.

charts.name: Top DMP Methylation Profiles by Group
charts.nameZh: Top DMP 的分组甲基化谱
charts.description: Methylation beta values of the six top-ranked DMPs, one panel per CpG: tumour (red) and normal (green) samples side by side with group medians; hyper-methylated candidates (cg00101-cg00112 style) separate cleanly, which is the property a methylation biomarker needs.

charts.name: ROC Validation of the Best-Separating CpG
charts.nameZh: 最优分离 CpG 的 ROC 验证
charts.description: ROC curve of the best-separating CpG as a single-marker tumour classifier: AUC 0.893 (95% CI 0.850-0.936) — strong separation from the planted hyper-methylation, though short of perfect; the marker box reports the AUC with its 95% confidence interval.

charts.name: Per-Subtype Amplification / Deletion Frequency Profiles
charts.type: Subtype-wise CNV Frequency Profiles with GISTIC Scores
charts.description: Copy-number alteration frequency per arm-level bin, one panel per subtype: amplification fraction (red, upward) and deletion fraction (blue, downward) across chromosomes 1-22; Subtype A peaks at 7q/20q amplification, Subtype B at 16q/18q deletion, and both share the low-level 8q gain.

charts.name: GISTIC-Style Scores with Arm-Level Peaks
charts.type: Subtype-wise CNV Frequency Profiles with GISTIC Scores
charts.description: GISTIC-style scores (amplitude x frequency, background-corrected) per bin for the two subtypes: dashed line marks the 0.10 score level; Subtype A's 7q/20q and Subtype B's 16q/18q peaks cross it while the shared 8q gain stays below — the subtype-specific drivers the per-subtype re-drawing exposes.

charts.name: Full-Locus Pileup and Coverage
charts.type: IGV-Style Read Pileup with Zoomed Base View
charts.description: IGV-style full-locus view: per-base coverage (top) over ~800 reads per sample drawn as thin strand-coloured rectangles in three lanes; at this zoom the G>A variant is a single invisible pixel — the reason IGV-style browsing needs the base-level zoom below.

charts.name: Base-Level Zoom at the Variant
charts.type: IGV-Style Read Pileup with Zoomed Base View
charts.description: IGV-style base-level zoom (60 bp around the G>A SNV): each read is a strand-coloured rectangle and mismatches are red bars; tumour lanes show the variant in roughly half their reads while the normal lane shows none — the allelic-fraction contrast the zoom exists to reveal.

charts.name: Matching (hand-implemented MatchIt equivalent)
charts.type: Propensity Score Matching (PSM) with Balance Diagnostics
charts.description: Propensity-score distributions before and after matching: before (top), controls (grey) spread far below the cases (red); after greedy 1:1 nearest matching (bottom), the matched controls sit on top of the cases — the covariate overlap PSM restores.

charts.name: Balance Diagnostics: Love Plot
charts.type: Propensity Score Matching (PSM) with Balance Diagnostics
charts.description: Love plot of standardized mean differences: age and male share before matching sit far above the 0.1 rule-of-thumb line, and matching pulls both under it — the covariate balance that licenses an outcome comparison.

charts.name: Zoomed Panel and Full View Side by Side
charts.nameZh: Zoomed Panel and Full View Side by Side
charts.type: Bubble Scatter with Base-Plot Zoom Panel
charts.description: Mutation-percentage bubbles in ILC vs IDC, base-plot zoom design: left panel enlarges the 0-15% corner (translucent highlight) where most genes pile up, right panel shows the full extent with a right-side axis; bubbles are coloured by functional group, sized by -log10(p), and labelled where space allows.

charts.name: The Fish Plot
charts.description: Clonal evolution fish plot over four time points (vertical lines): the root clone (green) carries the tumour through chemotherapy, two sub-clones (blue/red) emerge from it at the mid-treatment node, and the relapse clone (dark blue, nested inside sub-clone 2) expands at relapse; polygon thickness encodes each clone's fraction (polygon-style, linearly interpolated).

charts.name: Kappa Matrix Between Annotation Terms
charts.type: DAVID Kappa Matrix of Annotation Overlap
charts.description: Cohen's kappa between annotation terms over the 120 shared genes (clustered heatmap, values printed): the two planted near-duplicate pairs (mitotic cell cycle / cell cycle phase transition, innate immune response / cytokine signalling) reach kappa 0.77-0.82, while unrelated pairs stay below 0.2 — the redundancy DAVID's kappa is designed to expose.

charts.name: Term Sizes and Overlap Counts
charts.type: DAVID Kappa Matrix of Annotation Overlap
charts.description: Gene counts per annotation term (bars) with the kappa of each term's nearest neighbour printed above: near-duplicate pairs carry kappa > 0.8 while the lipid/oxidation-reduction pair's weak overlap shows as kappa ≈ 0.1 — pick one representative per high-kappa cluster before enrichment reporting.

charts.name: The Polar Ring
charts.description: ggplot2 polar circos over 180 genes: outer tiles colour-coded by copy-number state (red Gain / blue Loss / grey Neutral), inner scatter ring shows expression log2FC, and a thinned set of survival-flagged genes (S_) is labelled radially in black; the ring gap marks the chromosome-arm boundary.

charts.name: Concordance Check: CNV State vs Expression
charts.nameZh: 一致性检查：CNV 状态 vs 表达
charts.description: Mean expression log2FC by copy-number state: Gain genes average +1.1 and Loss genes -1.0 while Neutral genes sit at 0 — the CNV-expression concordance the ring encodes, with error bars as standard errors.

charts.name: Spearman Correlation Bubble Grid
charts.description: Spearman correlation of each candidate gene with each immune-cell ssGSEA score (colour = rho, size = -log10 p, stars = BH-significant): CD274 tracks CD8 T cells and macrophages (adaptive immune resistance), SIGLEC15 is macrophage-restricted, LAG3 is CD8-restricted and VEGFA tracks endothelial cells; TP53 and KRAS stay flat — the planted biology.

charts.name: CD274 Against Its Strongest Population
charts.description: CD274 expression vs CD8 T-cell ssGSEA score (Spearman rho = 0.78, p < 0.001): the adaptive-immune-resistance relationship behind the grid's strongest cell — the reference's per-pair follow-up scatter.

charts.name: ROAST Test Result
charts.type: ROAST Gene-Set Test with Barcode Plot
charts.description: ROAST results for the two signatures (DirectionDown/DirectionUp summaries, 500 rotations): the planted Notch signature is significant and up-directed (PValue 0.0017, FDR 0.003), while the inflammatory control set shows no directional enrichment — the hypothesis-driven gene-set test the reference uses.

charts.name: Barcode Plot Along the Moderated t Ranking
charts.nameZh: 沿 moderated t 排序的条码图
charts.type: ROAST Gene-Set Test with Barcode Plot
charts.description: Barcode plot: all 800 genes ranked by moderated t (treated vs control); red bars mark the 40 Notch-signature genes, the red trace above is the set's density along the ranking — massed on the positive-t side — and the mirrored trace below the confirm the up-direction; a Wilcoxon-style enrichment p is annotated.

charts.name: Paired Panels: Fold-Change Lines and Expression Boxes
charts.nameZh: 配对面板：倍数变化折线与表达箱线
charts.type: STEM Profile Panels with Pairwise-Significance Box Plots
charts.description: STEM profile panels (one column pair per profile): line plots of log2 fold change (grey genes, red representative) and box plots of absolute expression with adjacent-time-point Wilcoxon brackets and stars — the Rising profile climbs to 72 h, the Transient profile peaks at 6 h, and the Falling profile declines.

charts.name: Cluster-Annotated z-score Heatmap
charts.nameZh: 聚类注释的 z 分数热图
charts.description: STEM clusters as a z-scored heatmap (rows = 300 genes grouped by profile, columns = time points): the Rising block climbs to 72 h, the Transient block spikes at 6 h and decays, the Falling block declines; per-time-point mean traces (bottom panel) quantify each profile.

charts.name: Per-Profile Mean Traces
charts.description: Mean z-score per profile across the four time points (ribbons = ±1 SD): Rising peaks at 72 h (+2.4), Transient spikes at 6 h (+2.2) and decays, Falling declines monotonically to -2.5 — the three signatures the heatmap blocks encode.

charts.name: Two Genes Across the Immune-Sorted Sample Axis
charts.nameZh: 免疫排序样本轴上的双基因
charts.type: Dual-Axis Gene Expression with Immune High/Low Bands
charts.description: Two genes across samples sorted by gene A (immune-level bands in the background): gene A (left axis, blue) and gene B (right axis, red, scaled 4x) rise together inside the immune-high band and stay low in the immune-low band — the co-expression-with-immunity pattern the dual-axis design exposes.

charts.name: Matching the Reference: AIC Knot Selection
charts.nameZh: 匹配参考：AIC 节点选择
charts.type: Smoothed Hazard Ratio via Restricted Cubic Splines
charts.description: AIC across spline knot counts (nk = 3-6) for the rcs-Cox model: nk = 4 wins — the model-selection step the reference runs before drawing the HR curve.

charts.name: Smoothed HR Curve vs BMI
charts.nameZh: 平滑 HR 曲线 vs BMI
charts.type: Smoothed Hazard Ratio via Restricted Cubic Splines
charts.description: Smoothed hazard ratio of BMI relative to the reference (bmi = 25, dashed line at HR 1), from the AIC-selected 4-knot rcs-Cox model: both tails of the BMI distribution carry excess risk while the 23-27 band sits at HR 1 — the U-shape a single linear coefficient would average away; the log-scale y axis keeps the pointwise 95% CI band readable even in the sparse tails.

charts.name: 12 Cofactor Peak-Overlap Correlation (FigureYa115cofactor)
charts.description: Peak-overlap correlation between 8 ChIP-seq experiments: planted cofactor pairs (Meis1/Prep, Egr1/Nab2) reach r ≈ 0.7-0.8, the partial partner (Cbfb) sits near 0.4 and independent factors near 0 — corrplot ellipses (left) and the clustered pheatmap (right) agree on the grouping.

charts.name: Ring Layout with Category Arcs
charts.description: Bipartite arc diagram: outer arcs = glycan categories spanning their members, middle points = glycosides, inner rectangles = glycoproteins, connectors coloured by category. Targets are angle-ordered so connections read radially.

charts.name: deepTools-Style Aggregate Heatmap
charts.description: deepTools-style aggregate view: mean profiles per sample (left), per-region signal matrix grouped into 5 k-means-like classes (right), shared colour scale capped at zMax

charts.name: Rows Ordered by an External Grouping
charts.description: External-grouping layout: rows sorted by RNA-seq expression cluster (D1-D4), one signal panel per sample, heatmap + colour bar only

charts.name: Application: Donut Table for Cohort Balancing
charts.description: Cohort balancing table: each cell donuts one baseline feature within an arm; the bottom row gives the Fisher/chi-square p-value per feature

charts.name: Application: Three-Stage Mutation Flow
charts.description: Gene → mutation class → subtype flow from a long table: link width = number of events, ribbon colour = source node at 40% alpha

charts.name: Application: Grouped Marker Panels
charts.nameZh: 应用：按群体分组的标志基因面板
charts.description: matrixplot of dict-grouped markers: rectangle colour = scaled mean expression, one block per population

charts.name: Application: Grouped Marker Panels
charts.nameZh: 应用：按群体分组的标志基因面板
charts.description: tracksplot of the same dict: per-cell expression lines, cells grouped by population, one row per marker

charts.name: Outcome Comparison After Matching
charts.type: Propensity Score Matching (PSM) with Balance Diagnostics
charts.description: Quality-of-life difference (cancer patients minus population controls) before matching (all 250 cases vs all 1000 controls) and on the 250 matched pairs: with this simulated cohort age/sex confounding is mild (about 0.6 QoL points of the ~5.8-point gap), the balance diagnostics still have to decide whether the matched estimate is reported, and the 95% CIs show how much precision the 250-pair subset costs.

charts.name: 12 Cofactor Peak-Overlap Correlation (FigureYa115cofactor)
charts.description: The same correlation matrix as a clustered pheatmap with printed values: the cofactor pairs collapse into diagonal blocks — the clustering agrees with the ellipse reading.

charts.name: Application
charts.description: Three sets of KM curves

# Load the TCGA-BRCA gene expression dataset from a processed CSV file  
data_counts <- readr::read_csv("files/cos/TCGA-BRCA.htseq_counts_processed.csv")

# Load built-in R dataset iris
data_wide <- iris[ , 1:4] # Take the data in columns 1-4 of the iris database as an example

# Load built-in R dataset penguins
data("penguins", package = "palmerpenguins")
data_penguins <- drop_na(penguins) # Remove missing values

# Manually create a demonstration dataset with grouped values 
data <- data.frame(
  name=c( rep("A",500), rep("B",500), rep("B",500), rep("C",20), rep('D', 100)  ),
  value=c( rnorm(500, 10, 5), rnorm(500, 13, 1), rnorm(500, 18, 1), rnorm(20, 25, 4), rnorm(100, 12, 1) )
  )
sample_size <- data %>% 
  group_by(name) %>% 
  summarize(num=n()) # Compute the sample size for each group

# Basic Violin Plot
p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=name, y=value, fill=name)) + 
  geom_violin()

p

# Transform the `iris` dataset from wide format to long format. Use the gather function to collect the data in each column into two new columns named "MesureType" and "Val", so that one row represents one observation.
data_long_iris <- data_wide %>%  
  gather(key = "MeasureType", value = "Value")  

ggplot(data_long_iris, aes(x = MeasureType, y = Value, fill = MeasureType)) +  
  geom_violin()

example_counts1 <- data_counts[1:5,] %>%
  gather(key = "sample",value = "gene_expression",3:1219) # Select five example genes for visualization: A1BG, A1BG-AS1, A1CF, A2M, and A2M-AS1.

ggplot(example_counts1, aes(x=gene_name, y=gene_expression, fill=gene_name)) +
  geom_violin()

# Organize and group the data
data_long_iris <- data_wide %>%
  gather(key = "MeasureType",
         value = "Value")

# Draw a basic violin plot
p <- ggplot(data_long_iris,
       aes(x = MeasureType,
           y = Value,
           fill = MeasureType)) +
  geom_violin()

# Extract and deduplicate groups
groups <- length(unique(data_long_iris$MeasureType))
if (groups == 2) {
	p <- p +
		stat_compare_means(
			method = "wilcox.test", # c("t.test", "wilcox.test")
			paired = FALSE,
			method.args = list(),
			ref.group = NULL,
			comparisons = NULL,
			hide.ns = FALSE,
			label.sep = ", ",
			label = "p.format", # c("p.signif", "p.format")
			label.x.npc = "left",
			label.y.npc = "top",
			label.x = NULL,
			label.y = NULL,
			vjust = 0,
			tip.length = 0.03,
			bracket.size = 0.3,
			step.increase = 0.1,
			symnum.args = list(),
			geom = "text",
			position = "identity",
			na.rm = FALSE,
			show.legend = NA,
			inherit.aes = TRUE
		)
} else if (groups > 2) {
	p <- p +
		stat_compare_means(
			method = "wilcox.test", # c("t.test", "wilcox.test")
			paired = FALSE,
			method.args = list(),
			ref.group = NULL,
			# Perform pairwise comparisons for multiple group comparisons
			comparisons = combn(unique(as.character(data_long_iris$MeasureType)), 2, simplify = FALSE),
			hide.ns = FALSE,
			label.sep = ", ",
			label = "p.format", # c("p.signif", "p.format")
			label.x.npc = "left",
			label.y.npc = "top",
			label.x = NULL,
			label.y = NULL,
			vjust = 0,
			tip.length = 0.03,
			bracket.size = 0.3,
			step.increase = 0.1,
			symnum.args = list(),
			geom = "text",
			position = "identity",
			na.rm = FALSE,
			show.legend = NA,
			inherit.aes = TRUE
		)
}

p

# Separate the data for female and male penguins
data_female <- data_penguins %>% filter(sex == "female")

    aes(y = flipper_length_mm, x = species),
    colour = NA,
    fill = "#FFFF00",
    alpha = 0.6,
    side = "left", justification = 0, width = 0.8
  )

plt <- ggbetweenstats(

) +
# Beautification

  for (gn in seq_along(genes7)) {
    for (ag in seq_along(c("Y", "O"))) {
      base <- rnorm(24, mean = 2.2 + 0.4 * cl + 0.3 * gn, sd = 0.9)
      # marker gene: one cluster expresses high; old shifts up on the top marker
      if (gn == cl) base <- base + 2.3
      if (gn == 1 && cl == 1 && ag == 2) base <- base + 1.9
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        aging = c("Y", "O")[ag], cluster_short = clust[cl], gene = genes7[gn],
        expression = base, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}

library(rstatix)
set.seed(7301)
clust <- c("OO", "GC", "SC", "EC")
genes7 <- c("DDX4", "AMH", "COL1A2", "CDH5")
rows <- list()
for (cl in seq_along(clust)) {
  for (gn in seq_along(genes7)) {
    for (ag in seq_along(c("Y", "O"))) {
      base <- rnorm(24, mean = 2.2 + 0.4 * cl + 0.3 * gn, sd = 0.9)
      # marker gene: one cluster expresses high; old shifts up on the top marker
      if (gn == cl) base <- base + 2.3
      if (gn == 1 && cl == 1 && ag == 2) base <- base + 1.9
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        aging = c("Y", "O")[ag], cluster_short = clust[cl], gene = genes7[gn],
        expression = base, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
dfc <- do.call(rbind, rows)
dfc$aging <- factor(dfc$aging, levels = c("Y", "O"))
dfc$cluster_short <- factor(dfc$cluster_short, levels = clust)
dfc$gene <- factor(dfc$gene, levels = genes7)
# gate: the DDX4/OO facet is significantly higher in Old (the designed effect)
sub <- dfc[dfc$gene == "DDX4" & dfc$cluster_short == "OO", ]
wt <- wilcox.test(expression ~ aging, data = sub)
stopifnot(wt$p.value < 0.01 &&
          mean(sub$expression[sub$aging == "O"]) > mean(sub$expression[sub$aging == "Y"]))
stat_test <- dfc %>% group_by(cluster_short, gene) %>%
  wilcox_test(formula = expression ~ aging) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "bonferroni") %>%
  add_significance(p.col = "p.adj", cutpoints = c(0, 1e-4, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                   symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns")) %>%
  add_xy_position(x = "aging")
p_c <- ggviolin(dfc, x = "aging", y = "expression", fill = "aging", color = "aging",
                facet.by = c("gene", "cluster_short"), trim = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2874C5", "#EABF00"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2874C5", "#EABF00"), guide = "none") +
  stat_pvalue_manual(stat_test, hide.ns = TRUE, tip.length = 0,
                     label = "{p.adj} {p.adj.signif}", label.size = 2.6, vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 8),
        strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.background.x = element_rect(fill = "grey94", linewidth = 0, colour = NA),
        strip.background.y = element_rect(fill = "grey88", linewidth = 0, colour = NA),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") +
  labs(y = "Expression (log TPM)")
print(p_c)

set.seed(5501)
tissues <- c("BRCA", "COAD", "HNSC", "KIRC", "LUAD", "LUSC", "PRAD", "STAD", "THCA", "UCEC")
n_per <- 120
tp53_base <- c(BRCA = 2.6, COAD = 2.2, HNSC = 2.8, KIRC = 2.4, LUAD = 2.5,
               LUSC = 2.9, PRAD = 2.3, STAD = 2.7, THCA = 2.2, UCEC = 2.5)
pan <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  tumor <- rnorm(n_per, tp53_base[t] + 0.9, 0.75)
  normal <- rnorm(n_per, tp53_base[t] - 0.4, 0.6)
  rbind(data.frame(tissue = t, type2 = "tumor", tpm = tumor),
        data.frame(tissue = t, type2 = "normal", tpm = normal))
}))
pan$type2 <- factor(pan$type2, levels = c("tumor", "normal"))
pan$tissue <- factor(pan$tissue, levels = tissues)
pan$side <- ifelse(pan$type2 == "tumor", "right", "left")
wt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  d1 <- pan$tpm[pan$tissue == t & pan$type2 == "tumor"]
  d0 <- pan$tpm[pan$tissue == t & pan$type2 == "normal"]
  data.frame(tissue = t, p = wilcox.test(d1, d0)$p.value)
}))
star_df <- data.frame(tissue = factor(wt$tissue, levels = tissues),
                      y = max(pan$tpm) + 0.55,
                      lab = ifelse(wt$p < 0.001, "***",
                                   ifelse(wt$p < 0.01, "**",
                                          ifelse(wt$p < 0.05, "*", ""))))
## quartile marks: tiny horizontal dashes offset into each half
qd106 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("tumor", "normal"), function(g) {
  x <- pan$tpm[pan$tissue == t & pan$type2 == g]
  data.frame(tissue = t, type2 = g, q = quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)))
}))))
qd106$tissue <- factor(qd106$tissue, levels = tissues)
qd106$type2 <- factor(qd106$type2, levels = c("tumor", "normal"))
qd106$xc <- as.numeric(qd106$tissue) + ifelse(qd106$type2 == "tumor", 0.13, -0.13)

ggplot(pan, aes(tissue, tpm, fill = type2)) +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(aes(side = side), density = "bounded",
                       point_interval = NULL,
                       linewidth = 0.3, colour = "black", alpha = 0.95) +
  geom_segment(data = qd106,
               aes(x = xc - 0.025, xend = xc + 0.025, y = q, yend = q,
                   colour = type2),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.55) +
  geom_text(data = star_df, aes(tissue, y, label = lab),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4.2, colour = "grey10") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(tumor = "#DF2020", normal = "#DDDF21"), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(tumor = "#7a1010", normal = "#8a8a20"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2, max(pan$tpm) + 1.1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "TP53 expression (log2 TPM, simulated)",
       title = "Pan-cancer split violin: tumour vs matched normal (GTEx-like)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "top")

library(rstatix)
set.seed(7301)
clust <- c("OO", "GC", "SC", "EC")
genes7 <- c("DDX4", "AMH", "COL1A2", "CDH5")
rows <- list()
for (cl in seq_along(clust)) {
  for (gn in seq_along(genes7)) {
    for (ag in seq_along(c("Y", "O"))) {
      base <- rnorm(24, mean = 2.2 + 0.4 * cl + 0.3 * gn, sd = 0.9)
      # marker gene: one cluster expresses high; old shifts up on the top marker
      if (gn == cl) base <- base + 2.3
      if (gn == 1 && cl == 1 && ag == 2) base <- base + 1.9
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        aging = c("Y", "O")[ag], cluster_short = clust[cl], gene = genes7[gn],
        expression = base, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
dfc <- do.call(rbind, rows)
dfc$aging <- factor(dfc$aging, levels = c("Y", "O"))
dfc$cluster_short <- factor(dfc$cluster_short, levels = clust)
dfc$gene <- factor(dfc$gene, levels = genes7)
# gate: the DDX4/OO facet is significantly higher in Old (the designed effect)
sub <- dfc[dfc$gene == "DDX4" & dfc$cluster_short == "OO", ]
wt <- wilcox.test(expression ~ aging, data = sub)
stopifnot(wt$p.value < 0.01 &&
          mean(sub$expression[sub$aging == "O"]) > mean(sub$expression[sub$aging == "Y"]))
stat_test <- dfc %>% group_by(cluster_short, gene) %>%
  wilcox_test(formula = expression ~ aging) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "bonferroni") %>%
  add_significance(p.col = "p.adj", cutpoints = c(0, 1e-4, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                   symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns")) %>%
  add_xy_position(x = "aging")
p_c <- ggviolin(dfc, x = "aging", y = "expression", fill = "aging", color = "aging",
                facet.by = c("gene", "cluster_short"), trim = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2874C5", "#EABF00"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2874C5", "#EABF00"), guide = "none") +
  stat_pvalue_manual(stat_test, hide.ns = TRUE, tip.length = 0,
                     label = "{p.adj} {p.adj.signif}", label.size = 2.6, vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 8),

        axis.title.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") +

  tumor <- rnorm(n_per, tp53_base[t] + 0.9, 0.75)
  normal <- rnorm(n_per, tp53_base[t] - 0.4, 0.6)
  rbind(data.frame(tissue = t, type2 = "tumor", tpm = tumor),
        data.frame(tissue = t, type2 = "normal", tpm = normal))
}))
pan$type2 <- factor(pan$type2, levels = c("tumor", "normal"))
pan$tissue <- factor(pan$tissue, levels = tissues)
pan$side <- ifelse(pan$type2 == "tumor", "right", "left")
wt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  d1 <- pan$tpm[pan$tissue == t & pan$type2 == "tumor"]
  d0 <- pan$tpm[pan$tissue == t & pan$type2 == "normal"]
  data.frame(tissue = t, p = wilcox.test(d1, d0)$p.value)
}))
star_df <- data.frame(tissue = factor(wt$tissue, levels = tissues),
                      y = max(pan$tpm) + 0.55,
                      lab = ifelse(wt$p < 0.001, "***",

library(rstatix)
set.seed(7301)
clust <- c("OO", "GC", "SC", "EC")
genes7 <- c("DDX4", "AMH", "COL1A2", "CDH5")
rows <- list()
for (cl in seq_along(clust)) {
  for (gn in seq_along(genes7)) {
    for (ag in seq_along(c("Y", "O"))) {
      base <- rnorm(24, mean = 2.2 + 0.4 * cl + 0.3 * gn, sd = 0.9)
      # marker gene: one cluster expresses high; old shifts up on the top marker
      if (gn == cl) base <- base + 2.3
      if (gn == 1 && cl == 1 && ag == 2) base <- base + 1.9
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        aging = c("Y", "O")[ag], cluster_short = clust[cl], gene = genes7[gn],
        expression = base, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
dfc <- do.call(rbind, rows)
dfc$aging <- factor(dfc$aging, levels = c("Y", "O"))
dfc$cluster_short <- factor(dfc$cluster_short, levels = clust)
dfc$gene <- factor(dfc$gene, levels = genes7)
# gate: the DDX4/OO facet is significantly higher in Old (the designed effect)
sub <- dfc[dfc$gene == "DDX4" & dfc$cluster_short == "OO", ]
wt <- wilcox.test(expression ~ aging, data = sub)
stopifnot(wt$p.value < 0.01 &&
          mean(sub$expression[sub$aging == "O"]) > mean(sub$expression[sub$aging == "Y"]))
stat_test <- dfc %>% group_by(cluster_short, gene) %>%
  wilcox_test(formula = expression ~ aging) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "bonferroni") %>%
  add_significance(p.col = "p.adj", cutpoints = c(0, 1e-4, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                   symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns")) %>%
  add_xy_position(x = "aging")
p_c <- ggviolin(dfc, x = "aging", y = "expression", fill = "aging", color = "aging",
                facet.by = c("gene", "cluster_short"), trim = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2874C5", "#EABF00"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2874C5", "#EABF00"), guide = "none") +
  stat_pvalue_manual(stat_test, hide.ns = TRUE, tip.length = 0,
                     label = "{p.adj} {p.adj.signif}", label.size = 2.6, vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 8),

        strip.background.x = element_rect(fill = "grey94", linewidth = 0, colour = NA),
        strip.background.y = element_rect(fill = "grey88", linewidth = 0, colour = NA),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") +
  labs(y = "Expression (log TPM)")

library(rstatix)
set.seed(7301)
clust <- c("OO", "GC", "SC", "EC")
genes7 <- c("DDX4", "AMH", "COL1A2", "CDH5")
rows <- list()
for (cl in seq_along(clust)) {
  for (gn in seq_along(genes7)) {
    for (ag in seq_along(c("Y", "O"))) {
      base <- rnorm(24, mean = 2.2 + 0.4 * cl + 0.3 * gn, sd = 0.9)
      # marker gene: one cluster expresses high; old shifts up on the top marker
      if (gn == cl) base <- base + 2.3
      if (gn == 1 && cl == 1 && ag == 2) base <- base + 1.9
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        aging = c("Y", "O")[ag], cluster_short = clust[cl], gene = genes7[gn],
        expression = base, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
dfc <- do.call(rbind, rows)
dfc$aging <- factor(dfc$aging, levels = c("Y", "O"))
dfc$cluster_short <- factor(dfc$cluster_short, levels = clust)
dfc$gene <- factor(dfc$gene, levels = genes7)
# gate: the DDX4/OO facet is significantly higher in Old (the designed effect)
sub <- dfc[dfc$gene == "DDX4" & dfc$cluster_short == "OO", ]
wt <- wilcox.test(expression ~ aging, data = sub)
stopifnot(wt$p.value < 0.01 &&
          mean(sub$expression[sub$aging == "O"]) > mean(sub$expression[sub$aging == "Y"]))
stat_test <- dfc %>% group_by(cluster_short, gene) %>%
  wilcox_test(formula = expression ~ aging) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "bonferroni") %>%
  add_significance(p.col = "p.adj", cutpoints = c(0, 1e-4, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                   symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns")) %>%
  add_xy_position(x = "aging")
p_c <- ggviolin(dfc, x = "aging", y = "expression", fill = "aging", color = "aging",
                facet.by = c("gene", "cluster_short"), trim = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2874C5", "#EABF00"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2874C5", "#EABF00"), guide = "none") +
  stat_pvalue_manual(stat_test, hide.ns = TRUE, tip.length = 0,
                     label = "{p.adj} {p.adj.signif}", label.size = 2.6, vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 8),
        strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.background.x = element_rect(fill = "grey94", linewidth = 0, colour = NA),
        strip.background.y = element_rect(fill = "grey88", linewidth = 0, colour = NA),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") +
  labs(y = "Expression (log TPM)")
print(p_c)

set.seed(5501)
tissues <- c("BRCA", "COAD", "HNSC", "KIRC", "LUAD", "LUSC", "PRAD", "STAD", "THCA", "UCEC")
n_per <- 120
tp53_base <- c(BRCA = 2.6, COAD = 2.2, HNSC = 2.8, KIRC = 2.4, LUAD = 2.5,
               LUSC = 2.9, PRAD = 2.3, STAD = 2.7, THCA = 2.2, UCEC = 2.5)
pan <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  tumor <- rnorm(n_per, tp53_base[t] + 0.9, 0.75)
  normal <- rnorm(n_per, tp53_base[t] - 0.4, 0.6)
  rbind(data.frame(tissue = t, type2 = "tumor", tpm = tumor),
        data.frame(tissue = t, type2 = "normal", tpm = normal))
}))
pan$type2 <- factor(pan$type2, levels = c("tumor", "normal"))
pan$tissue <- factor(pan$tissue, levels = tissues)
pan$side <- ifelse(pan$type2 == "tumor", "right", "left")
wt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  d1 <- pan$tpm[pan$tissue == t & pan$type2 == "tumor"]
  d0 <- pan$tpm[pan$tissue == t & pan$type2 == "normal"]
  data.frame(tissue = t, p = wilcox.test(d1, d0)$p.value)
}))
star_df <- data.frame(tissue = factor(wt$tissue, levels = tissues),
                      y = max(pan$tpm) + 0.55,
                      lab = ifelse(wt$p < 0.001, "***",
                                   ifelse(wt$p < 0.01, "**",
                                          ifelse(wt$p < 0.05, "*", ""))))
## quartile marks: tiny horizontal dashes offset into each half
qd106 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("tumor", "normal"), function(g) {
  x <- pan$tpm[pan$tissue == t & pan$type2 == g]
  data.frame(tissue = t, type2 = g, q = quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)))
}))))
qd106$tissue <- factor(qd106$tissue, levels = tissues)
qd106$type2 <- factor(qd106$type2, levels = c("tumor", "normal"))
qd106$xc <- as.numeric(qd106$tissue) + ifelse(qd106$type2 == "tumor", 0.13, -0.13)

ggplot(pan, aes(tissue, tpm, fill = type2)) +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(aes(side = side), density = "bounded",
                       point_interval = NULL,
                       linewidth = 0.3, colour = "black", alpha = 0.95) +
  geom_segment(data = qd106,
               aes(x = xc - 0.025, xend = xc + 0.025, y = q, yend = q,
                   colour = type2),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.55) +
  geom_text(data = star_df, aes(tissue, y, label = lab),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4.2, colour = "grey10") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(tumor = "#DF2020", normal = "#DDDF21"), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(tumor = "#7a1010", normal = "#8a8a20"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2, max(pan$tpm) + 1.1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "TP53 expression (log2 TPM, simulated)",
       title = "Pan-cancer split violin: tumour vs matched normal (GTEx-like)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "top")

  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#BDD7E7", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = observed, colour = "#B2182B", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = observed - 1.2,
           y = max(table(random_hits)) * 0.9, hjust = 1, colour = "#B2182B", size = 3.4,
           label = sprintf("Observed = %d\nEmpirical p %s",
                           observed, ifelse(p_emp < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", p_emp)))) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Over-expressed genes among %d random draws", N_de),
       y = "Frequency in simulations",
       title = sprintf("%d Monte-Carlo simulations", N_sim)) +

set.seed(42)
genes9 <- paste0("Gene", 1:8)
stage  <- factor(rep(paste0("stage", 1:3), each = 10))

expr9 <- sapply(seq_along(genes9), function(g) {
  eff <- if (g %in% c(2, 5)) c(0, 1.5, 3) else c(0, 0, 0)  # stage-dependent genes
  rnorm(30, mean = 3 + eff[stage], sd = 0.8)
})
colnames(expr9) <- genes9

long9 <- data.frame(stage = stage, expr9) |>
  pivot_longer(-stage, names_to = "gene", values_to = "expr")

# One-way ANOVA per gene + significance stars
sig9 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genes9, function(g) {
  p <- summary(aov(expr ~ stage, data = subset(long9, gene == g)))[[1]]$"Pr(>F)"[1]
  data.frame(gene = g,
             label = paste0("ANOVA p ",
                            ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", p)), " ",
                            cut(p, c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                                labels = c("***", "**", "*", ""))))
}))

ymax9 <- tapply(long9$expr, long9$gene, max)

ggplot(long9, aes(x = stage, y = expr, fill = stage)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = sig9,
            aes(x = 2, y = ymax9[gene] + 0.5, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~gene, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#BDD7E7", "#6BAED6", "#2171B5")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative expression (log2)") +

  eff <- if (g %in% c(2, 5)) c(0, 1.5, 3) else c(0, 0, 0)  # stage-dependent genes
  rnorm(30, mean = 3 + eff[stage], sd = 0.8)

             label = paste0("ANOVA p ",
                            ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", p)), " ",
                            cut(p, c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                                labels = c("***", "**", "*", ""))))

genes9 <- paste0("Gene", 1:8)

expr9 <- sapply(seq_along(genes9), function(g) {
  eff <- if (g %in% c(2, 5)) c(0, 1.5, 3) else c(0, 0, 0)  # stage-dependent genes
  rnorm(30, mean = 3 + eff[stage], sd = 0.8)
})
colnames(expr9) <- genes9

  pivot_longer(-stage, names_to = "gene", values_to = "expr")

# One-way ANOVA per gene + significance stars

  p <- summary(aov(expr ~ stage, data = subset(long9, gene == g)))[[1]]$"Pr(>F)"[1]
  data.frame(gene = g,
             label = paste0("ANOVA p ",
                            ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", p)), " ",
                            cut(p, c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                                labels = c("***", "**", "*", ""))))
}))

ymax9 <- tapply(long9$expr, long9$gene, max)

  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +

set.seed(404)
clusters <- c("C1", "C2", "C3")
n_per <- 30
sig_sets <- list(
  `Immune checkpoint` = paste0("ICG", 1:15),
  `Antigen processing` = paste0("APM", 1:15),
  `TGF-beta response` = paste0("TGF", 1:15)
)
all_genes <- unlist(sig_sets)
meta <- data.frame(sample = paste0("S", 1:90),
                   cluster = rep(clusters, each = n_per))

expr10 <- matrix(rnorm(45 * 90, sd = 1), nrow = 45, dimnames = list(all_genes, meta$sample))
shift <- c(0, 0.7, 1.6)[match(meta$cluster, clusters)]      # C3 strongest
for (gs in c("Immune checkpoint", "Antigen processing")) {
  expr10[sig_sets[[gs]], ] <- sweep(expr10[sig_sets[[gs]], ], 2, shift, "+")  # shift applies per sample (column)
}
expr10[sig_sets[["TGF-beta response"]], meta$cluster == "C3"] <-
  expr10[sig_sets[["TGF-beta response"]], meta$cluster == "C3"] - 1.2

## sign-corrected PC1 score per signature (the reference workflow's core step)
score_of <- function(gs) {
  m <- expr10[sig_sets[[gs]], , drop = FALSE]
  pc <- prcomp(t(m), retx = TRUE)
  pc$x[, 1] * sign(cor(pc$x[, 1], colMeans(m)))
}
scores <- sapply(names(sig_sets), score_of)

long10 <- data.frame(sample = meta$sample, cluster = meta$cluster, scores) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(sample, cluster), names_to = "Signature", values_to = "Score") |>
  mutate(Score = as.numeric(scale(Score)))

ggplot(long10, aes(Signature, Score, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.65) +
  stat_compare_means(label = "p.signif", method = "kruskal.test") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E31A1C", "#E7B800", "#2E9FDF")) +
  labs(y = "Signature score (scaled)", fill = "TME cluster") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

)

                   cluster = rep(clusters, each = n_per))

expr10 <- matrix(rnorm(45 * 90, sd = 1), nrow = 45, dimnames = list(all_genes, meta$sample))
