bases <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")
dye_colours <- c(A = "#2E8B57", C = "#2166AC", G = "#222222", T = "#C51B1F")
n_base <- 96

called <- sample(bases, n_base, replace = TRUE, prob = c(.3, .2, .22, .28))
called[61] <- "Y"                       # C/T heterozygote
called[88:96] <- sample(bases, 9, replace = TRUE)

position <- seq_len(n_base)
base_amp <- rnorm(n_base, 860, 55)
base_amp[61] <- 900
scan <- seq(1, n_base, length.out = n_base * 24)
peak <- function(centre, sigma = 0.30) {
  dnorm(scan, centre, sigma) / dnorm(centre, centre, sigma)
}

## Each channel carries a peak only where that base was called. The C/T site
## receives two half-height peaks, which is the evidence a heterozygote call needs.
make_channel <- function(ch) {
  y <- numeric(length(scan))
  for (i in seq_along(called)) {
    if (called[i] == ch) y <- y + base_amp[i] * peak(i)
    if (called[i] == "Y" && ch %in% c("C", "T")) {
      y <- y + 0.58 * base_amp[i] * peak(i)
    }
  }
  y
}

  mutate(A = make_channel("A"), C = make_channel("C"),

  pivot_longer(-scan, names_to = "channel", values_to = "signal") |>
  mutate(
    base_index = scan,

## A chromosome table in the shape RIdeogram expects: name, start, end,
## centromere. Lengths are a five-chromosome toy genome in Mb.
karyo <- data.frame(
  chr = c("chr1", "chr2", "chr3", "chr4", "chr5"),
  len = c(120, 95, 80, 60, 45),
  cen = c(48, 34, 31, 21, 17)
)
set.seed(43501)

## Cytobands: alternating stain with a density value, as G-band tables carry.
banding <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(karyo)), function(i) {
  k <- karyo[i, ]
  starts <- seq(0, k$len, by = 6)
  data.frame(chr = k$chr, start = starts, end = pmin(starts + 6, k$len),
             density = round(runif(length(starts), 0, 100)))
}))

## Per-window Fst with two planted peaks, so the reading order is verifiable.
win <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(karyo)), function(i) {
  k <- karyo[i, ]
  mid <- seq(1, k$len - 1, by = 2)
  fst <- 0.08 + 0.05 * abs(sin(mid / 9))
  if (k$chr == "chr2") fst <- fst + 0.55 * exp(-((mid - 62)^2) / 40)
  if (k$chr == "chr4") fst <- fst + 0.42 * exp(-((mid - 20)^2) / 50)
  data.frame(chr = k$chr, mid = mid,
             fst = pmin(0.95, fst + rnorm(length(mid), 0, 0.02)))
}))

## Coordinates are compressed to a schematic axis: each exon keeps its length,
## the introns are shortticks, and both partners are drawn left-to-right.
make_model <- function(exons, y, gap_scale = 0.04) {
  intron_len <- diff(exons$start)
  ## Schematic bp = exon lengths + a squashed intron of fixed visual width.
  exon_len <- exons$end - exons$start + 1
  offset <- c(0, cumsum(exon_len + max(exon_len) * gap_scale))[seq_len(nrow(exons))]
  tibble(exon = exons$exon, x0 = offset, x1 = offset + exon_len, y = y)
}

tx_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(tx), function(t) {
  ids <- tx[[t]]

  e$x0 <- cumsum(c(0, (e$gend - e$gstart + gap)[-nrow(e)]))

    0.9 * exp(-((p - peak_at)^2) / (2 * 180^2)) +
    rnorm(length(p), 0, 0.03)

build_map <- function(n_chr, n_mar, hotspot_centre, hotspot_width) {
  span_mb <- 120
  ## Recombination rate r(x) in cM/Mb: baseline 1, a Gaussian hotspot cluster,
  ## and a cold centromere.
  dx <- seq(0, span_mb, length.out = 4001)
  r_rate <- 0.35 + 120 * dnorm(dx, hotspot_centre, hotspot_width) -
    0.25 * dnorm(dx, 60, 10)
  r_rate <- pmax(r_rate, 0.04)
  cum_cm <- cumsum(r_rate) * (span_mb / (length(dx) - 1))
  ## Physical positions of n_mar markers equally spaced in cM.
  cm_of <- seq(0, max(cum_cm), length.out = n_mar)
  pos_mb <- approx(cum_cm, dx, xout = cm_of, rule = 2)$y
  tibble(chr = n_chr, marker = seq_len(n_mar), cM = cm_of, Mb = pos_mb,
         marker_name = sprintf("M%03d", seq_len(n_mar)))
}

maps <- bind_rows(
  build_map(n_chr = 1, n_mar = 60, hotspot_centre = 85, hotspot_width = 3.5) |>
    mutate(species = "Species A"),
  build_map(n_chr = 1, n_mar = 60, hotspot_centre = 40, hotspot_width = 7) |>
    mutate(species = "Species B")
)

## Local recombination rate from the map itself: d(cM)/d(Mb) between adjacent
## markers — the only quantity a linkage map can actually estimate.
## The rate is evaluated on a fine physical grid (bins of ~1.5 Mb): two
## adjacent markers can be a few kb apart inside a hotspot and 10 Mb apart in a
## cold region, so a marker-to-marker ratio would be dominated by noise.
rate_grid <- function(dx, cum_cm, width = 1.5) {
  ## Bin EDGES on the physical grid, so every bin spans exactly `width` Mb and
  ## rate = dC / width is the true average over that span. A finer grid
  ## (step < width) would give bins covering less than `width` Mb and bias
  ## every rate down by the same factor.
  brk <- seq(0, max(dx), by = width)
  bin <- cut(dx, breaks = c(brk, max(dx) + width), include.lowest = TRUE,
             labels = FALSE)

    rate = vapply(idx[keep], function(ii) diff(range(cum_cm[ii])) /

build_map <- function(n_chr, n_mar, hotspot_centre, hotspot_width) {
  span_mb <- 120
  ## Recombination rate r(x) in cM/Mb: baseline 1, a Gaussian hotspot cluster,
  ## and a cold centromere.
  dx <- seq(0, span_mb, length.out = 4001)
  r_rate <- 0.35 + 120 * dnorm(dx, hotspot_centre, hotspot_width) -
    0.25 * dnorm(dx, 60, 10)
  r_rate <- pmax(r_rate, 0.04)
  cum_cm <- cumsum(r_rate) * (span_mb / (length(dx) - 1))
  ## Physical positions of n_mar markers equally spaced in cM.
  cm_of <- seq(0, max(cum_cm), length.out = n_mar)
  pos_mb <- approx(cum_cm, dx, xout = cm_of, rule = 2)$y
  tibble(chr = n_chr, marker = seq_len(n_mar), cM = cm_of, Mb = pos_mb,
         marker_name = sprintf("M%03d", seq_len(n_mar)))
}

## Local recombination rate from the map itself: d(cM)/d(Mb) between adjacent
## markers — the only quantity a linkage map can actually estimate.
## The rate is evaluated on a fine physical grid (bins of ~1.5 Mb): two
## adjacent markers can be a few kb apart inside a hotspot and 10 Mb apart in a
## cold region, so a marker-to-marker ratio would be dominated by noise.
rate_grid <- function(dx, cum_cm, width = 1.5) {
  ## Bin EDGES on the physical grid, so every bin spans exactly `width` Mb and
  ## rate = dC / width is the true average over that span. A finer grid
  ## (step < width) would give bins covering less than `width` Mb and bias
  ## every rate down by the same factor.
  brk <- seq(0, max(dx), by = width)
  bin <- cut(dx, breaks = c(brk, max(dx) + width), include.lowest = TRUE,
             labels = FALSE)
  idx <- split(seq_along(dx), bin)
  keep <- vapply(idx, function(ii) {
    !is.na(ii[1]) && length(ii) > 1 && diff(range(dx[ii])) > 0.5 * width
  }, logical(1))
  data.frame(
    Mb_mid = vapply(idx[keep], function(ii) mean(range(dx[ii])), numeric(1)),
    rate = vapply(idx[keep], function(ii) diff(range(cum_cm[ii])) /
                    diff(range(dx[ii])), numeric(1))
  )
}

  ## cum_cm as a function of physical position, from the map itself, on a

  grid <- seq(0, max(sub$Mb), by = 0.5)
  cm <- approx(sub$Mb, sub$cM, xout = grid, rule = 2)$y
  rate_grid(grid, cm) |> mutate(species = sp)
}))

set.seed(43511)

## Toy genome: five chromosomes with a SNP panel every ~200 kb, laid on a
## cumulative axis so that runs can cross chromosome boundaries nowhere.
chr <- data.frame(chr = paste0("chr", 1:5), len = c(120, 95, 80, 60, 45),
                  offset = c(0, 124, 223, 307, 371))
snp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(chr)), function(i) {
  n <- round(chr$len[i] / 0.2)
  data.frame(chr = chr$chr[i], pos = sort(runif(n, 0, chr$len[i])))
}))
snp$x <- snp$pos + chr$offset[match(snp$chr, chr$chr)]

## Per-sample homozygosity at the 62% background rate, then planted patterns:
## two genome-wide (consanguinity), one focal run, one patchy intermediate set.
samples <- sprintf("S%02d", 1:12)
hz <- expand.grid(sample = samples, id = seq_len(nrow(snp))) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(chr = snp$chr[id], x = snp$x[id], hom = runif(n()) < 0.62) |>

## Haplotype simulation by segment-wise founder copying. Breakpoints split
## the locus into segments; within a segment every simulated haplotype copies
## one of four founder haplotypes, with a small per-site error rate. Blocks of
## high LD therefore appear by construction, and D' / r^2 are computed from
## the resulting 0/1/2 dosage matrix — no value is painted into the figure.
simulate_pop <- function(n_ind, breaks, e = 0.001, mut = 0.001) {
  ## Breakpoints split the locus into segments; each simulated haplotype
  ## copies one founder haplotype within a segment. That is the standard
  ## four-founder / ancestral-haplotype caricature of LD. The founder pool
  ## is deliberately close to two ancestral states: f1 is all reference,
  ## f2 is all alternate, and f3/f4 carry rare derived alleles.
  segment <- cumsum(c(TRUE, seq_len(n_snp - 1) %in% breaks))
  n_seg <- max(segment)
  n_hap <- 120
  f1 <- rep(0L, n_snp)
  f2 <- rep(1L, n_snp)
  f3 <- f1; f3[runif(n_snp) < mut] <- 1L
  f4 <- f2; f4[runif(n_snp) < mut] <- 0L
  founder <- rbind(f1, f2, f3, f4)
  hap <- matrix(0L, n_hap, n_snp)
  for (k in seq_len(n_hap)) {
    for (seg in seq_len(n_seg)) {
      cols <- which(segment == seg)
      ## Draw a founder independently for every segment. A deterministic
      ## rotation would preserve the same haplotype across a breakpoint and
      ## silently erase the very LD boundary the example is meant to show.
      h <- sample.int(4, 1)
      hap[k, cols] <- founder[h, cols]
      flip <- which(runif(length(cols)) < e)
      hap[k, cols[flip]] <- 1L - hap[k, cols[flip]]
    }
  }
  a <- matrix(sample(seq_len(n_hap), n_ind * 2, replace = TRUE), n_ind, 2)
  list(hap = hap, segment = segment,
       geno = hap[a[, 1], , drop = FALSE] + hap[a[, 2], , drop = FALSE])
}

## D' and r^2 from a 0/1/2 dosage matrix (the formula used by PLINK --r2 and
## LDBlockShow): p_A, p_B from allele frequencies, D from joint haplotypes
## estimated by the composite ( EM-free ) count from genotypes.
ld_pair <- function(g1, g2) {
  ## g = 0/1/2 dosage. Cov(dosage1, dosage2) = 2 D, so D = Cov / 2.
  f1 <- mean(g1) / 2; f2 <- mean(g2) / 2
  if (f1 %in% c(0, 1) || f2 %in% c(0, 1)) return(c(Dprime = NA_real_, r2 = NA_real_))
  d <- stats::cov(g1, g2) / 2
  denom <- if (d >= 0) min(f1 * (1 - f2), (1 - f1) * f2) else
    min(f1 * f2, (1 - f1) * (1 - f2))
  dprime <- if (denom > 0) abs(d) / denom else NA_real_
  r2 <- d^2 / (f1 * (1 - f1) * f2 * (1 - f2))
  c(Dprime = min(dprime, 1), r2 = min(r2, 1))
}

}

## Block calling on the composite LD measure: a boundary is a SNP pair whose
## linkage falls below the strong-LD threshold (a Gabriel-style composite
## rule; Gabriel et al. themselves use confidence bounds on D', not r^2).
blocks_of <- function(dat, thr = 0.7) {
  d <- filter(dat, j == i + 1) |>
    mutate(strong = !is.na(Dprime) & !is.na(r2) & Dprime > thr & r2 > 0.45)
  ## Consecutive strong pairs belong to the same block.
  block_id <- cumsum(c(TRUE, diff(d$i) > 1 | !d$strong[-length(d$strong)]))
  tibble(i = d$i, block = block_id) |>
    mutate(block = as.integer(factor(block)))
}

## Per-population block boundaries. A boundary between SNP b and b+1 is
## drawn as a vertical line spanning the upper triangle (j > b).
block_edges <- block_bounds |>
  group_by(pop) |>
  arrange(i) |>
  mutate(new_block = block != lag(block)) |>
  filter(!is.na(new_block) & new_block) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(pop, i0 = i, j0 = i + 1, j1 = n_snp)

p_ld <- ggplot(ld, aes(i, j)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = r2), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.18) +
  geom_segment(data = block_edges,
               aes(x = i0, xend = i0, y = j0, yend = j1),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#1f4e79", linewidth = 0.45,
               linetype = "22") +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#ffffff", "#c6dbef", "#6baed6", "#2171b5",
                                   "#08306b"),
                       limits = c(0, 1), values = c(0, .2, .45, .7, 1),
                       na.value = "grey92", name = expression(r^2)) +
  ## No coord_fixed() here: the fixed aspect squeezed the two facets into
  ## the middle of the panel while p_gene filled the full width, so SNP k in
  ## the heatmaps sat at a different x than SNP k in the gene track.
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, n_snp, 5), limits = c(0.5, n_snp + 0.5),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +

  facet_wrap(~pop, ncol = 1) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 9.5) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),

        axis.text = element_text(size = 7.8),

  mutate(gene_id = row_number(),
         ## Alternate labels above / below the baseline so adjacent gene
         ## names never collide at this density.

         lab_x = if_else(gene_id %% 2 == 1, start + 0.1, end - 0.1),

## Four chromosomes, 12 admixed individuals from three source populations, and
## one 25 Mb archaic haplotype shared by five of them. Tracts are drawn from a
## 1 Mb Markov chain with a 3% switch rate (switches often re-draw the same
## ancestry, so realised tracts run to tens of Mb).
chroms <- data.frame(chr = paste0("chr", 1:4), len = c(180, 160, 140, 120))
inds <- sprintf("IND%02d", 1:12)
groups <- rep(c("AFR", "EUR", "NAT"), each = 4)
props <- list(AFR = c(AFR = .80, EUR = .15, NAT = .05),
              EUR = c(AFR = .10, EUR = .85, NAT = .05),
              NAT = c(AFR = .05, EUR = .10, NAT = .85))

tracts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(inds, function(id) {
  g <- groups[match(id, inds)]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(chroms)), function(k) {
    n <- chroms$len[k]
    st <- character(n)
    cur <- sample(names(props[[g]]), 1, prob = props[[g]])
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      if (i > 1 && runif(1) < 0.03) cur <- sample(names(props[[g]]), 1, prob = props[[g]])
      st[i] <- cur
    }
    data.frame(ind = id, chr = chroms$chr[k], start = seq_len(n) - 1,
               end = seq_len(n), anc = st,
               run = cumsum(c(TRUE, st[-1] != st[-n])))
  }))
}))

## Collapse consecutive equal calls into one tract per run.
tracts <- tracts |>
  group_by(ind, chr, run) |>
  summarise(anc = first(anc), start = min(start), end = max(end), .groups = "drop")

## Plant the archaic haplotype: five carriers, chr2:60-85 Mb. Tracts that
## overlap the interval are split at its boundaries, not deleted: deleting a
## whole tract would leave the rest of that chromosome unpainted.
carriers <- c("IND01", "IND03", "IND05", "IND08", "IND11")
is_carrier <- function(d) d$ind %in% carriers & d$chr == "chr2"
left <- tracts |> filter(is_carrier(tracts), start < 60) |> mutate(end = pmin(end, 60))
right <- tracts |> filter(is_carrier(tracts), end > 85) |> mutate(start = pmax(start, 85))
seg <- tracts |> filter(!is_carrier(tracts)) |>
  bind_rows(left, right,
            data.frame(ind = carriers, chr = "chr2", anc = "ARCH",
                       start = 60, end = 85, run = 999)) |>
  mutate(anc = factor(anc, levels = c("AFR", "EUR", "NAT", "ARCH"))) |>
  arrange(ind, chr, start)

pal_anc <- c(AFR = "#4c72b0", EUR = "#dd8452", NAT = "#55a868", ARCH = "#c44e52")
ypos <- setNames(seq_along(inds), inds)
seg$y <- ypos[seg$ind]

ggplot(seg) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = y - 0.42, ymax = y + 0.42,
                fill = anc)) +
  facet_grid(~ chr, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_anc, name = "ancestry") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(inds), labels = inds, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.07))) +
  labs(x = "position within chromosome (Mb)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.6),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal",
        legend.key.height = unit(0.22, "cm"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.6),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 6.8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

## Population-level ancestry proportion along chr2: the mean over the 12
## individuals in each 1 Mb window. The archaic block is the step at 60-85 Mb.
d2 <- filter(seg, chr == "chr2")
## Population-level proportion = mean over the 12 individuals, each counted
## once. Taking the mean over tract rows would silently weight individuals by
## how many tracts they happen to carry (here 28 rows for 12 people).
carriers <- function(a, pos) mean(vapply(unique(d2$ind), function(id)
  any(d2$anc == a & d2$ind == id & d2$start <= pos & d2$end > pos), logical(1)))
win <- data.frame(pos = 0:159) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(AFR = carriers("AFR", pos),
         EUR = carriers("EUR", pos),
         NAT = carriers("NAT", pos),
         ARCH = carriers("ARCH", pos)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pivot_longer(c(AFR, EUR, NAT, ARCH), names_to = "anc", values_to = "frac") |>
  mutate(anc = factor(anc, levels = c("AFR", "EUR", "NAT", "ARCH")))

ggplot(win, aes(pos, frac, fill = anc)) +
  geom_area(position = "stack", colour = NA) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 60, xmax = 85, ymin = 0, ymax = 1,
           fill = NA, colour = "#c44e52", linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = 72.5, y = 1.04, label = "archaic haplotype",
           size = 2.4, colour = "#c44e52") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_anc, name = "ancestry") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0.005, 0.005)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), limits = c(0, 1.12)) +
  labs(x = "chr2 position (Mb)", y = "ancestry proportion") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.direction = "horizontal", legend.key.height = unit(0.22, "cm"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.6), legend.title = element_text(size = 6.8))

## Coancestry from the same tracts: the fraction of 1 Mb bins in which two
## individuals carry the same ancestry label, clustered by 1 - similarity.
state_vec <- function(id) {
  unlist(lapply(chroms$chr, function(ch) {
    a <- seg |> filter(ind == id, chr == ch) |> arrange(start)
    v <- rep(NA_character_, chroms$len[chroms$chr == ch])
    for (k in seq_len(nrow(a))) v[(a$start[k] + 1):a$end[k]] <- as.character(a$anc[k])
    v
  }))
}
states <- setNames(lapply(inds, state_vec), inds)
co <- expand.grid(ind1 = inds, ind2 = inds, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
co$same <- mapply(function(a, b) mean(states[[a]] == states[[b]], na.rm = TRUE),
                  co$ind1, co$ind2)
mat <- co |> pivot_wider(names_from = ind2, values_from = same) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("ind1") |> as.matrix()
ord <- hclust(as.dist(1 - mat), method = "average")$order
co$ind1 <- factor(co$ind1, levels = inds[ord])
co$ind2 <- factor(co$ind2, levels = inds[ord])
co$same <- ifelse(co$ind1 == co$ind2, NA, co$same)

ggplot(co, aes(ind1, ind2, fill = same)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradientn("shared\nancestry",
                       colours = c("#f7f7f7", "#fdae6b", "#a63603"),
                       limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "#e0e0e0") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 5.6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.6), panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.key.height = unit(0.7, "cm"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.2),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 6.6))

## Coancestry from the same tracts: the fraction of 1 Mb bins in which two
## individuals carry the same ancestry label, clustered by 1 - similarity.
state_vec <- function(id) {
  unlist(lapply(chroms$chr, function(ch) {
    a <- seg |> filter(ind == id, chr == ch) |> arrange(start)
    v <- rep(NA_character_, chroms$len[chroms$chr == ch])
    for (k in seq_len(nrow(a))) v[(a$start[k] + 1):a$end[k]] <- as.character(a$anc[k])
    v
  }))
}
states <- setNames(lapply(inds, state_vec), inds)

co$same <- mapply(function(a, b) mean(states[[a]] == states[[b]], na.rm = TRUE),
                  co$ind1, co$ind2)
mat <- co |> pivot_wider(names_from = ind2, values_from = same) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("ind1") |> as.matrix()
ord <- hclust(as.dist(1 - mat), method = "average")$order
co$ind1 <- factor(co$ind1, levels = inds[ord])
co$ind2 <- factor(co$ind2, levels = inds[ord])
co$same <- ifelse(co$ind1 == co$ind2, NA, co$same)

ggplot(co, aes(ind1, ind2, fill = same)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradientn("shared\nancestry",

chr_len <- 620
sentinel <- 412.6          # Mb

## Variants in a 1.2 Mb window around the sentinel. r2 decays with distance
## (the colour channel); -log10 P carries two signals, one of which is only in
## LD with the sentinel because it is physically close.
reg <- data.frame(pos = seq(sentinel - 0.6, sentinel + 0.6, by = 0.004)) |>
  mutate(
    r2 = pmax(0, 1 - abs(pos - sentinel) / 0.62)^1.6,
    lp = -log10(pmax(1e-12, pmin(0.9,
      10^(-(2.1 + 6.4 * exp(-((pos - sentinel)^2) / (2 * 0.05^2)) +
              3.4 * exp(-((pos - (sentinel + 0.33))^2) / (2 * 0.035^2)) +
              runif(n()) * 1.6)))))
  )

genes <- data.frame(
  gene = c("GENEA", "GENEB", "GENEC", "GENED"),
  start = c(sentinel - 0.55, sentinel - 0.12, sentinel + 0.18, sentinel + 0.42),
  end   = c(sentinel - 0.35, sentinel + 0.06, sentinel + 0.40, sentinel + 0.57)
)
genes$mid <- (genes$start + genes$end) / 2
exons <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(genes)), function(i) {
  g <- genes[i, ]
  data.frame(gene = g$gene,
             x0 = seq(g$start, g$end - 0.02, length.out = 3),
             x1 = seq(g$start, g$end - 0.02, length.out = 3) + 0.025)
}))

rec <- data.frame(pos = seq(sentinel - 0.6, sentinel + 0.6, by = 0.01)) |>
  mutate(
    ## a recombination hotspot sits between the two signals, which is why they
    ## are in separate LD blocks
    cmmb = 0.8 + 1.6 * exp(-((pos - (sentinel + 0.16))^2) / (2 * 0.012^2)) +
      0.35 * exp(-((pos - (sentinel - 0.3))^2) / (2 * 0.08^2))
  )

  mutate(ld = cut(r2, breaks = c(-Inf, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, Inf),

         is_sentinel = abs(pos - sentinel) < 0.0015)

  scale_colour_manual(values = ld_cols, name = expression(r^2), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(reg$lp) + 1.6), expand = c(0, 0),

## One locus: 60 CpG sites and 24 reads. Reads are split into two haplotypes;
## sites 20-34 are a differentially methylated region (DMR), so the figure has
## a signal that a per-site average would blur away.
n_sites <- 60
n_reads <- 24
reads <- sprintf("read_%02d", 1:n_reads)
hap <- rep(c("hap1", "hap2"), each = n_reads / 2)

bg <- 0.55 + 0.22 * sin(seq_len(n_sites) / 6)
p_h1 <- bg
p_h2 <- bg
p_h1[20:34] <- 0.92
p_h2[20:34] <- 0.10

## Per-read, per-site methylation calls. `cov` is FALSE where the read has no
## call: random dropout plus a low-coverage stretch at sites 44-50.
meth <- expand.grid(site = seq_len(n_sites), read = reads, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  mutate(hap = hap[match(read, reads)],
         mu = ifelse(hap == "hap1", p_h1[site], p_h2[site]),
         meth = pmin(1, pmax(0, rbeta(n(), mu * 9, (1 - mu) * 9))),
         cov = !(runif(n()) < 0.08 | (site %in% 44:50 & runif(n()) < 0.6)))

## Per-site coverage and mean methylation, plus the hap1-only summary used by
## the sorted ladder. A site passes at 10x (all reads) or 5x (hap1 reads).
site_sum <- meth |>
  filter(cov) |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(cov_n = n(), mean_meth = mean(meth), .groups = "drop") |>
  right_join(data.frame(site = seq_len(n_sites)), by = "site") |>
  mutate(cov_n = ifelse(is.na(cov_n), 0L, cov_n),
         pass = cov_n >= 10)

site_h1 <- meth |>
  filter(cov, hap == "hap1") |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(cov_n = n(), mean_meth = mean(meth), .groups = "drop") |>
  right_join(data.frame(site = seq_len(n_sites)), by = "site") |>
  mutate(cov_n = ifelse(is.na(cov_n), 0L, cov_n),
         pass = cov_n >= 5,
         ci = qnorm(0.975) * sqrt(mean_meth * (1 - mean_meth) / pmax(cov_n, 1)),
         lo = pmax(0, mean_meth - ci),
         hi = pmin(1, mean_meth + ci)) |>
  arrange(mean_meth) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number())

## Position probability matrix for a 24-nt stem-loop: a GC-rich stem
## (4-8 paired with 17-21), an 8-nt loop (9-16) and two unpaired flanks.
pfm <- matrix(0.025, nrow = 4, ncol = 24,
              dimnames = list(c("A", "C", "G", "U"), NULL))
pfm[1, 1:3] <- c(0.7, 0.1, 0.1)
pfm[2, 1:3] <- c(0.1, 0.7, 0.1)
pfm[3, 1:3] <- c(0.1, 0.1, 0.7)
pfm[4, 1:3] <- c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
for (k in 1:5) {                       # stem: G-C x 3, then A-U, G-C
  b <- list(c("G", "C"), c("G", "C"), c("G", "C"), c("A", "U"),
            c("G", "C"))[[k]]
  pfm[, 3 + k] <- 0.025
  pfm[b[1], 3 + k] <- 0.85
  pfm[b[2], 16 + k] <- 0.85
  pfm[b[2], 3 + k] <- 0.05
  pfm[b[1], 16 + k] <- 0.05
}
for (k in 9:13) {                      # loop
  pfm[, k] <- c(0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
}
pfm[, 14:15] <- c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25)
pfm <- sweep(pfm, 2, colSums(pfm), "/")

## Information content per column (bits, max 2 for RNA).
ic <- apply(pfm, 2, function(p) 2 + sum(p * log2(p)))
letters_df <- as.data.frame(pfm) |>
  rownames_to_column("base") |>
  pivot_longer(-base, names_to = "col", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(col = as.integer(sub("V", "", col)),
         ic = ic[col],
         h = p * ic) |>
  filter(p > 0.02) |>
  arrange(col, h) |>
  group_by(col) |>
  mutate(stack = cumsum(h), mid = stack - h / 2) |>
  ungroup()

## Pairing table: five supported stem pairs plus one weak candidate.
pairs <- data.frame(
  i = c(4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10),
  j = c(21, 20, 19, 18, 17, 15),
  support = c("supported", "supported", "supported", "supported",
              "supported", "weak")
)

arc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(k) {
  p <- pairs[k, ]
  t <- seq(0, pi, length.out = 60)
  span <- p$j - p$i
  data.frame(x = p$i + span * (1 - cos(t)) / 2,
             y = 2.9 + span * 0.08 * sin(t) + k * 0.02,
             support = p$support, id = k)
}))

## Seven homologous blocks with their lengths in Mb, and five genome
## assemblies described as ordered block lists. G2 transposes E and D, G3 has
## lost E, G4 inverts B and C, and G4/G5 differ from G1 in total length by
## +10% and -15% so that the normalisation question has a visible answer.
blocks <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G")
blen <- c(A = 1.20, B = 0.85, C = 0.60, D = 0.95, E = 0.45, F = 0.70, G = 0.55)

order_list <- list(
  G1 = list(b = blocks, o = rep("+", 7)),
  G2 = list(b = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "D", "F", "G"), o = rep("+", 7)),
  G3 = list(b = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F", "G"), o = rep("+", 6)),
  G4 = list(b = c("A", "C", "B", "D", "E", "F", "G"), o = c("+", "-", "-", rep("+", 4))),
  G5 = list(b = blocks, o = rep("+", 7))
)
scale_factor <- c(G1 = 1.00, G2 = 1.00, G3 = 1.00, G4 = 1.10, G5 = 0.85)
genomes <- names(order_list)

## Cumulative coordinates, per-genome total and percent-of-genome position.

  e <- order_list[[g]]
  data.frame(genome = g, block = e$b, orientation = e$o,
             len = blen[e$b] * scale_factor[[g]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})) |>
  group_by(genome) |>
  mutate(x0 = cumsum(c(0, len[-n()])), x1 = cumsum(len),
         total = sum(len), mid = (x0 + x1) / 2) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(genome) |>
  mutate(p0 = 100 * x0 / total, p1 = 100 * x1 / total) |>
  ungroup()

## Tracks are stacked with a fixed gap; integer y ranges keep blank space out.
gap <- 0.55
track_h <- 0.42
tot <- ord |> group_by(genome) |> summarise(total = first(total), .groups = "drop")
off <- setNames(cumsum(c(0, tot$total[-nrow(tot)] + gap)), tot$genome)

pal <- c(A = "#4c72b0", B = "#dd8452", C = "#55a868", D = "#c44e52",
         E = "#8172b3", F = "#937860", G = "#da8bc3")

## Ribbons between adjacent genomes: a quadrilateral per shared block. When the
## orientation differs the bottom edge is reversed, so the ribbon crosses.
ribbon_pairs <- function(a, b) {
  A <- ord |> filter(genome == a)
  B <- ord |> filter(genome == b)
  m <- merge(A, B, by = "block", suffixes = c(".a", ".b"))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(m)), function(i) {
    a0 <- c(m$x0.a[i], m$x1.a[i])
    b0 <- c(m$x0.b[i], m$x1.b[i])
    inv <- m$orientation.a[i] != m$orientation.b[i]
    ## x order (a-left, a-right, b-right, b-left) gives a simple quadrilateral;
    ## for an inversion the b edge is NOT reversed, so the ribbon self-crosses
    ## into a bow-tie -- the crossing IS the orientation signal.
    x <- if (inv) c(a0, b0) else c(a0, rev(b0))
    data.frame(grp = paste0(a, "-", i), x = x,
               y = c(m$y1.a[i], m$y1.a[i], m$y0.b[i], m$y0.b[i]), inv = inv)
  }))
}

## Concentric rings (BRIG layout) plus chords between the outermost ring (G1)
## and the inverted genome (G4). Each ring starts at 12 o'clock and runs
## clockwise over the same 360° sweep: ring position is percent-of-genome,
## so boundaries are NOT radially aligned across rings of unequal genomes.
ring_r <- c(G1 = 1.00, G2 = 0.92, G3 = 0.84, G4 = 0.76, G5 = 0.68)
ring_w <- 0.05
th0 <- 90
sweep <- 360
ang <- function(p) th0 - sweep * p / 100
d2r <- function(d) d * pi / 180

arc_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ord)), function(i) {
  a <- ord[i, ]
  th <- seq(ang(a$p0), ang(a$p1), length.out = 60)
  th[1] <- th[1] - 0.4              # 0.8° gap so adjacent blocks stay separate
  th[length(th)] <- th[length(th)] + 0.4
  r <- ring_r[[a$genome]]
  data.frame(grp = paste0(a$genome, a$block), block = a$block,
             x = c(r * cos(d2r(th)), (r - ring_w) * rev(cos(d2r(th)))),
             y = c(r * sin(d2r(th)), (r - ring_w) * rev(sin(d2r(th)))))
}))

ch <- merge(ord |> filter(genome == "G1") |> select(block, p0.a = p0, p1.a = p1),
            ord |> filter(genome == "G4") |> select(block, p0.b = p0, p1.b = p1),
            by = "block") |>
  mutate(inv = block %in% c("B", "C"))
chord_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ch)), function(i) {
  s <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 40)
  p0a <- ch$p0.a[i]; p1a <- ch$p1.a[i]; p0b <- ch$p0.b[i]; p1b <- ch$p1.b[i]
  if (ch$inv[i]) { tmp <- p0b; p0b <- p1b; p1b <- tmp }
  r0 <- ring_r[["G1"]]; r1 <- ring_r[["G4"]]
  px <- function(p, r) c(r * cos(d2r(ang(p))), r * sin(d2r(ang(p))))
  A <- cbind(px(p0a, r0), px(p1a, r0))
  B <- cbind(px(p0b, r1), px(p1b, r1))
  bez <- function(p, q, ctrl = 0.6) {
    cx <- ctrl * (p[1] + q[1]) / 2
    cy <- ctrl * (p[2] + q[2]) / 2
    cbind((1 - s)^2 * p[1] + 2 * (1 - s) * s * cx + s^2 * q[1],
          (1 - s)^2 * p[2] + 2 * (1 - s) * s * cy + s^2 * q[2])
  }
  e1 <- bez(A[, 1], B[, 1])
  e2 <- bez(A[, 2], B[, 2])
  data.frame(grp = paste0("c", i), block = ch$block[i], inv = ch$inv[i],
             x = c(e1[, 1], rev(e2[, 1])), y = c(e1[, 2], rev(e2[, 2])))
}))

p_circle <- ggplot() +

## The same two genomes on an absolute axis and on a percent-of-genome axis.
## G4 is 10% longer than G1, so on the absolute axis its track runs to 5.83 Mb;
## on the normalised axis both tracks end exactly at 100%.
long <- rbind(
  ord |> transmute(genome, block, measure = "absolute (Mb)", lo = x0, hi = x1, pos = (x0 + x1) / 2),
  ord |> transmute(genome, block, measure = "percent of genome", lo = p0, hi = p1, pos = (p0 + p1) / 2)
)

make_panel <- function(meas, x_lim, subtitle) {
  d <- filter(long, measure == meas)
  m <- merge(filter(d, genome == "G1"), filter(d, genome == "G4"), by = "block")
  links <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(m)), function(i) {
    inv <- m$block[i] %in% c("B", "C")
    b0 <- c(m$lo.y[i], m$hi.y[i])
    ## Same vertex rule as figure 1: reverse the far edge only when the block
    ## is collinear, so inversions render as crossing ribbons.
    if (!inv) b0 <- rev(b0)
    data.frame(grp = i, inv = inv, x = c(m$lo.x[i], m$hi.x[i], b0),
               y = c(3.6, 3.6, 2.4, 2.4))
  }))
  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = links, aes(x, y, group = grp, fill = inv),
                 alpha = 0.45, colour = NA) +
    geom_rect(data = filter(d, genome == "G1"), aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, ymin = 3.6, ymax = 4.0, fill = block),
              colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.92) +
    geom_rect(data = filter(d, genome == "G4"), aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, ymin = 2.0, ymax = 2.4, fill = block),
              colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.92) +
    geom_text(data = filter(d, genome == "G1"), aes(pos, 3.8, label = block),
              size = 2.3, colour = "#111111") +
    geom_text(data = filter(d, genome == "G4"), aes(pos, 2.2, label = block),
              size = 2.3, colour = "#111111") +
    annotate("text", x = -0.01 * x_lim, y = c(3.8, 2.2), label = c("G1", "G4"),
             hjust = 1, size = 2.7, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = x_lim * 0.5, y = 4.2, label = subtitle,
             size = 2.5, colour = "#333333") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(pal, `TRUE` = "#e08214", `FALSE` = "#bdbdbd"),
                      guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, x_lim), ylim = c(1.9, 4.3), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = meas, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          plot.margin = margin(2, 8, 2, 30))
}

  G1 = list(b = blocks, o = rep("+", 7)),

  G4 = list(b = c("A", "C", "B", "D", "E", "F", "G"), o = c("+", "-", "-", rep("+", 4))),
  G5 = list(b = blocks, o = rep("+", 7))

  mutate(x0 = cumsum(c(0, len[-n()])), x1 = cumsum(len),

## Ribbons between adjacent genomes: a quadrilateral per shared block. When the
## orientation differs the bottom edge is reversed, so the ribbon crosses.
ribbon_pairs <- function(a, b) {
  A <- ord |> filter(genome == a)
  B <- ord |> filter(genome == b)
  m <- merge(A, B, by = "block", suffixes = c(".a", ".b"))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(m)), function(i) {
    a0 <- c(m$x0.a[i], m$x1.a[i])
    b0 <- c(m$x0.b[i], m$x1.b[i])
    inv <- m$orientation.a[i] != m$orientation.b[i]
    ## x order (a-left, a-right, b-right, b-left) gives a simple quadrilateral;
    ## for an inversion the b edge is NOT reversed, so the ribbon self-crosses
    ## into a bow-tie -- the crossing IS the orientation signal.
    x <- if (inv) c(a0, b0) else c(a0, rev(b0))
    data.frame(grp = paste0(a, "-", i), x = x,
               y = c(m$y1.a[i], m$y1.a[i], m$y0.b[i], m$y0.b[i]), inv = inv)
  }))
}

## Eight orthologues of a 60-residue fragment: positions 1-25 and 40-52 are
## conserved (the two secondary-structure elements the strip will mark).
aa <- strsplit("ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY", "")[[1]]
classes <- c(A = "h", V = "h", I = "h", L = "h", M = "h", F = "a", W = "a",
             Y = "a", S = "p", T = "p", N = "p", Q = "p", C = "p", G = "t",
             P = "t", D = "n", E = "n", K = "b", R = "b", H = "b")

prot <- matrix(sample(aa, 8 * 60, replace = TRUE), nrow = 8)
conserved <- c(1:25, 40:52)
for (p in conserved) {
  keep <- sample(aa, 1)
  prot[, p] <- keep                            # fully conserved columns
}
## two columns are conserved only at class level
for (p in c(28, 55)) {
  cls <- sample(c("h", "p", "b"), 1)
  prot[, p] <- sample(names(classes)[classes == cls], 8, replace = TRUE)
}
rownames(prot) <- sprintf("SPECIES_%d", 1:8)

  rownames_to_column("seq") |>
  pivot_longer(-seq, names_to = "col", values_to = "residue") |>
  mutate(col = as.integer(sub("V", "", col)),
         row = as.integer(sub("SPECIES_", "", seq)))

## Conservation per column: identity (all residues equal) or class identity.
cons <- long |>
  group_by(col) |>
  summarise(n_res = n_distinct(residue),
            n_cls = n_distinct(classes[residue]), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(level = case_when(n_res == 1 ~ "identical",
                           n_cls == 1 ~ "class",
                           TRUE ~ "none"))

  mutate(is_ident = !is.na(level) & level == "identical")

## ALT allele matrix: clade-specific variants are near-fixed in their clade,
## background variants appear at 25%.
snp <- matrix(0L, nrow = n_strain, ncol = n_var,
              dimnames = list(strains, paste0("v", seq_len(n_var))))
for (j in seq_len(n_var)) {
  snp[, j] <- if (var_clade[j] == "random") {
    rbinom(n_strain, 1, 0.25)
  } else {
    as.integer(clade == var_clade[j] & runif(n_strain) < 0.9)
  }
}

## Average-linkage tree from the binary variant distance.
hc <- hclust(dist(snp, method = "binary"), method = "average")
tip_order <- hc$order
n <- length(tip_order)
ypos <- setNames(seq_len(n), strains[tip_order])

## Convert the dendrogram to a segment table: leaves at x = root height, root
## at x = 0. The same table drives the rectangular and the circular tree.
mid_of <- function(node) {
  if (is.leaf(node)) return(unname(ypos[[attr(node, "label")]]))
  mean(c(mid_of(node[[1]]), mid_of(node[[2]])))
}
seg_from <- function(node, parent_h) {
  if (is.leaf(node)) {
    y <- ypos[[attr(node, "label")]]
    return(data.frame(x0 = parent_h, x1 = 0, y0 = y, y1 = y))
  }
  h <- attr(node, "height")
  c1 <- node[[1]]
  c2 <- node[[2]]
  m1 <- mid_of(c1)
  m2 <- mid_of(c2)
  rbind(seg_from(c1, h), seg_from(c2, h),
        data.frame(x0 = c(parent_h, h), x1 = c(h, h),
                   y0 = c(mid_of(node), m1), y1 = c(mid_of(node), m2)))
}

## Convert the dendrogram to a segment table: leaves at x = root height, root
## at x = 0. The same table drives the rectangular and the circular tree.
mid_of <- function(node) {
  if (is.leaf(node)) return(unname(ypos[[attr(node, "label")]]))
  mean(c(mid_of(node[[1]]), mid_of(node[[2]])))
}
seg_from <- function(node, parent_h) {
  if (is.leaf(node)) {
    y <- ypos[[attr(node, "label")]]
    return(data.frame(x0 = parent_h, x1 = 0, y0 = y, y1 = y))
  }
  h <- attr(node, "height")
  c1 <- node[[1]]
  c2 <- node[[2]]
  m1 <- mid_of(c1)
  m2 <- mid_of(c2)
  rbind(seg_from(c1, h), seg_from(c2, h),
        data.frame(x0 = c(parent_h, h), x1 = c(h, h),
                   y0 = c(mid_of(node), m1), y1 = c(mid_of(node), m2)))
}

             NheI = 2305, SalI = 4220, KpnI = 4260, PstI = 4300)
for (en in names(planted)) {
  p <- planted[[en]]
  site <- enzymes$site[enzymes$enzyme == en]
  seq_char[p:(p + nchar(site) - 1)] <- strsplit(site, "")[[1]]
}

reverse_complement <- function(x) {
  chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", paste(rev(strsplit(x, "")[[1]]), collapse = ""))
}

find_sites <- function(site, sequence) {
  hits <- gregexpr(site, sequence, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  hits <- hits[hits > 0]
  rc <- gregexpr(reverse_complement(site), sequence, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  rc <- rc[rc > 0]
  sort(unique(c(hits, rc)))
}

}

## A strand-aware block arrow on a circle of radius r, returning ONE closed
## polygon per feature (body + head), so a white outline never cuts the head
## off from the body.
ring_arrow <- function(start, end, r, half, strand, n_pt = 40) {
  if (end < start) end <- end + plasmid_len        # feature wraps the origin
  ## On a clockwise circle, the arrow head must sit at the 3' end in the
  ## direction of travel: increasing bp for +, decreasing bp for -.
  head <- max((end - start) * 0.26, 1)
  arc <- function(from, to) seq(from, to, length.out = n_pt)

  if (strand > 0) {
    outer <- data.frame(bp = arc(start, end - head), r = r + half)
    barb_out <- data.frame(bp = c(end - head, end - head), r = c(r + half, r + half * 1.9))
    apex <- data.frame(bp = end, r = r)
    barb_in <- data.frame(bp = c(end - head, end - head), r = c(r - half * 1.9, r - half))
    inner <- data.frame(bp = rev(arc(start, end - head)), r = r - half)
  } else {
    ## Travel from `end` (5' in bp terms) back toward `start`; the head
    ## therefore points at decreasing bp.
    outer <- data.frame(bp = arc(end, start + head), r = r + half)
    barb_out <- data.frame(bp = c(start + head, start + head), r = c(r + half, r + half * 1.9))
    apex <- data.frame(bp = start, r = r)
    barb_in <- data.frame(bp = c(start + head, start + head), r = c(r - half * 1.9, r - half))
    inner <- data.frame(bp = rev(arc(end, start + head)), r = r - half)
  }

  poly <- rbind(outer, barb_out, apex, barb_in, inner)
  poly$deg <- bp_to_deg(poly$bp)
  poly
}

}

reverse_complement <- function(x) {
  chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", paste(rev(strsplit(x, "")[[1]]), collapse = ""))
}

find_sites <- function(site, sequence) {
  hits <- gregexpr(site, sequence, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  hits <- hits[hits > 0]
  rc <- gregexpr(reverse_complement(site), sequence, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  rc <- rc[rc > 0]
  sort(unique(c(hits, rc)))
}

## A strand-aware block arrow on a circle of radius r, returning ONE closed
## polygon per feature (body + head), so a white outline never cuts the head
## off from the body.
ring_arrow <- function(start, end, r, half, strand, n_pt = 40) {
  if (end < start) end <- end + plasmid_len        # feature wraps the origin
  ## On a clockwise circle, the arrow head must sit at the 3' end in the
  ## direction of travel: increasing bp for +, decreasing bp for -.
  head <- max((end - start) * 0.26, 1)
  arc <- function(from, to) seq(from, to, length.out = n_pt)

  if (strand > 0) {
    outer <- data.frame(bp = arc(start, end - head), r = r + half)
    barb_out <- data.frame(bp = c(end - head, end - head), r = c(r + half, r + half * 1.9))
    apex <- data.frame(bp = end, r = r)
    barb_in <- data.frame(bp = c(end - head, end - head), r = c(r - half * 1.9, r - half))
    inner <- data.frame(bp = rev(arc(start, end - head)), r = r - half)
  } else {
    ## Travel from `end` (5' in bp terms) back toward `start`; the head
    ## therefore points at decreasing bp.
    outer <- data.frame(bp = arc(end, start + head), r = r + half)
    barb_out <- data.frame(bp = c(start + head, start + head), r = c(r + half, r + half * 1.9))
    apex <- data.frame(bp = start, r = r)
    barb_in <- data.frame(bp = c(start + head, start + head), r = c(r - half * 1.9, r - half))
    inner <- data.frame(bp = rev(arc(end, start + head)), r = r - half)
  }

  poly <- rbind(outer, barb_out, apex, barb_in, inner)
  poly$deg <- bp_to_deg(poly$bp)
  poly
}

}))

               py = c(y + height / 2, y + height / 2, y, y - height / 2, y - height / 2))

## A 200 kb tandem array made of 1 kb units. Three unit types are laid out in
## blocks; the type-1 block at 0-60 kb is duplicated at 100-160 kb, which is the
## higher-order repeat a self-similarity plot is meant to reveal.
K <- 9
alpha <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")
make_unit <- function() {
  paste(sample(alpha, 1000, replace = TRUE, prob = c(.3, .2, .2, .3)), collapse = "")
}
types <- replicate(3, make_unit())
unit_type <- c(rep(1, 60), rep(2, 40), rep(1, 60), rep(3, 40))

set.seed(4352)

## 1-based coordinates of three constitutive exons and one cassette exon
exons <- tibble(
  exon   = c("E1", "E2", "E3", "E4"),
  start  = c(1000, 1800, 2400, 3300),
  end    = c(1200, 1980, 2580, 3560)
)

samples <- c("Brain_1", "Brain_2", "Liver_1", "Liver_2")
group   <- c("Brain", "Brain", "Liver", "Liver")

cov <- expand_grid(pos = seq(900, 3700, by = 10), sample = samples) |>
  mutate(
    in_exon = (pos >= 1000 & pos <= 1200) | (pos >= 1800 & pos <= 1980) |
      (pos >= 2400 & pos <= 2580) | (pos >= 3300 & pos <= 3560),
    group = group[match(sample, samples)]
  )

## E3 is ~6x deeper in brain because the inclusion isoform dominates there
cov <- cov |>
  mutate(
    depth = ifelse(
      in_exon,
      ifelse(pos >= 2400 & pos <= 2580,
             ifelse(group == "Brain", 260, 40),
             ifelse(group == "Brain", 210, 200)),
      rpois(n(), 2)
    ),
    depth = pmax(0, round(depth + rnorm(n(), 0, 8)))
  )

junctions <- tribble(
  ~donor, ~acceptor, ~strand, ~sample, ~reads,
  1200, 1800, "+", "Brain_1", 412,
  1200, 1800, "+", "Brain_2", 388,
  1200, 1800, "+", "Liver_1", 455,
  1200, 1800, "+", "Liver_2", 431,
  1980, 2400, "+", "Brain_1", 356,
  1980, 2400, "+", "Brain_2", 341,
  1980, 2400, "+", "Liver_1",  38,
  1980, 2400, "+", "Liver_2",  29,
  2580, 3300, "+", "Brain_1", 331,
  2580, 3300, "+", "Brain_2", 318,
  2580, 3300, "+", "Liver_1",  12,
  2580, 3300, "+", "Liver_2",   9,
  ## exon-skipping junction E2 -> E4, dominant in liver
  1980, 3300, "+", "Brain_1",  21,
  1980, 3300, "+", "Brain_2",  17,
  1980, 3300, "+", "Liver_1", 392,
  1980, 3300, "+", "Liver_2", 410,
  ## antisense junction on the opposite strand, low but real; on a minus-strand
  ## transcript the donor (5' splice site) carries the HIGHER coordinate
  1980, 1200, "-", "Brain_1",  34,
  1200, 1980, "-", "Brain_2",  28,
  1200, 1980, "-", "Liver_1",  31,
  1200, 1980, "-", "Liver_2",  26
) |>
  mutate(group = group[match(sample, samples)])

junction_means <- junctions |>
  group_by(group, donor, acceptor, strand) |>
  summarise(reads = mean(reads), .groups = "drop")

junction_means

arc_points <- function(donor, acceptor, y0, height, n = 60) {
  t <- seq(0, pi, length.out = n)
  tibble(pos = donor + (acceptor - donor) * (1 - cos(t)) / 2,
         y = y0 + height * sin(t))
}

cov_scaled <- cov |>
  group_by(sample) |>
  mutate(depth_rel = depth / max(depth)) |>
  ungroup()

tracks <- cov_scaled |>
  distinct(sample, group) |>
  arrange(group, sample) |>
  mutate(y_base = -row_number() * 1.25)

cov_scaled <- cov_scaled |>
  left_join(tracks, by = c("sample", "group")) |>
  mutate(y = y_base + depth_rel)

## One arc per junction per SAMPLE, scaled by that sample's own read count --
## joining the tissue means on the tissue-level table would duplicate each
## arc onto both replicates and weld the copies into one long path.
arcs <- junctions |>
  inner_join(tracks, by = c("sample", "group")) |>
  mutate(height = (0.15 + 0.55 * reads / max(reads)) * ifelse(strand == "+", 1, -1))

arc_df <- arcs |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(pts = list(arc_points(donor, acceptor, y_base, height))) |>
  unnest(pts) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = cov_scaled,
              aes(pos, ymin = y_base, ymax = y, fill = group, group = sample),
              alpha = 0.28, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(data = cov_scaled,
            aes(pos, y, colour = group, group = sample), linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_path(data = arc_df,
            aes(pos, y, group = interaction(donor, acceptor, sample, strand),
                linetype = strand, linewidth = reads),
            colour = "#2B2B2B", alpha = 0.9, lineend = "round") +
  geom_segment(data = exons, aes(x = start, xend = end, y = 0.35, yend = 0.35),
               linewidth = 2.8, colour = "#1B1B1B") +
  geom_text(data = exons, aes(x = (start + end) / 2, y = 0.62, label = exon),
            size = 2.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Brain = "#2166AC", Liver = "#B2182B"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Brain = "#2166AC", Liver = "#B2182B"),
                      name = "Group (coverage)") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`+` = "solid", `-` = "22"),
                        labels = c(`+` = "+ strand", `-` = "- strand"),
                        name = "Junction strand") +
  scale_linewidth_continuous(range = c(0.25, 2.0), name = "Junction reads") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = tracks$y_base + 0.45, labels = tracks$sample,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.10, 0.06))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Genomic position (bp, chr1)",
    y = "Relative coverage per sample (reads, normalised per track)",
    title = "Cassette exon E3 is included in brain and skipped in liver",
    subtitle = "Arc thickness = supporting junction reads; arcs above the baseline are + strand, below are - strand"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.key.height = unit(3.4, "mm"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#4D4D4D", size = 9),

## PSI is defined here with E2-E3 as the inclusion junction and E2-E4 as the
## skipping junction. An alternative definition that also counts E3-E4 would
## sum the two inclusion junctions; the caption states the definition used.
psi <- junctions |>
  filter(strand == "+", donor == 1980) |>
  mutate(event = ifelse(acceptor == 2400, "inclusion", "skipping")) |>
  group_by(sample, group, event) |>
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(sample, group) |>
  summarise(
    inclusion = reads[event == "inclusion"],
    skipping  = reads[event == "skipping"],
    psi       = inclusion / (inclusion + skipping),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

arc_points <- function(donor, acceptor, y0, height, n = 60) {
  t <- seq(0, pi, length.out = n)
  tibble(pos = donor + (acceptor - donor) * (1 - cos(t)) / 2,
         y = y0 + height * sin(t))
}

cov_scaled <- cov |>
  group_by(sample) |>
  mutate(depth_rel = depth / max(depth)) |>
  ungroup()

tracks <- cov_scaled |>
  distinct(sample, group) |>
  arrange(group, sample) |>
  mutate(y_base = -row_number() * 1.25)

  left_join(tracks, by = c("sample", "group")) |>
  mutate(y = y_base + depth_rel)

## joining the tissue means on the tissue-level table would duplicate each
## arc onto both replicates and weld the copies into one long path.
arcs <- junctions |>
  inner_join(tracks, by = c("sample", "group")) |>
  mutate(height = (0.15 + 0.55 * reads / max(reads)) * ifelse(strand == "+", 1, -1))

                    levels = c("Malignant", "Non-malignant"))
cells <- paste0(substr(cell_type, 1, 3), "_", sprintf("%03d", seq_len(2 * n_mal)))

expr <- matrix(rnorm(n_gene * length(cells), mean = 5, sd = 0.5),
               nrow = n_gene, dimnames = list(genes, cells))
## broad CNV waves in malignant cells: sinusoid per chromosome,
## amplitude and phase vary per cell
for (i in seq_len(n_mal)) {
  for (chr in seq_len(n_chr)) {
    amp   <- runif(1, 0.4, 1.0) * sample(c(-1, 1), 1)        # del or amp
    phase <- runif(1, 0, 2 * pi)
    idx   <- which(gene_pos$chr == chr)
    expr[idx, i] <- expr[idx, i] +
      amp * sin(seq_along(idx) / length(idx) * 2 * pi + phase)
  }
}

## gene ordering + centring + bounding (the reference recipe)
gene_order <- order(gene_pos$chr, gene_pos$idx)
expr <- expr[gene_order, ]
rela <- sweep(expr, 1, rowMeans(expr))
rela <- pmin(pmax(rela, -3), 3)

smoothed <- rela
for (c_idx in seq_len(ncol(rela))) {
  smoothed[, c_idx] <- data.table::frollmean(rela[, c_idx], n = 50, align = "center")
}
smoothed[is.na(smoothed)] <- 0
## per-cell median re-centring after smoothing (Patel et al., 2014)
smoothed <- sweep(smoothed, 2, apply(smoothed, 2, median))

cnv_score <- colMeans(smoothed^2)
col_order <- order(cell_type, -cnv_score)

col_fun <- circlize::colorRamp2(c(-1.5, 0, 1.5), c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))
row_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  df = data.frame(Type = cell_type[col_order],
                  `CNV score` = cnv_score[col_order]),
  col = list(Type = c(Malignant = "#B2182B", `Non-malignant` = "#4D4D4D")),
  annotation_name_side = "left")

Heatmap(smoothed[, col_order], name = "CNV",
        top_annotation = row_ha,
        col = col_fun,
        cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_columns = FALSE,
        show_column_names = FALSE, show_row_names = FALSE,
        column_split = cell_type[col_order], column_gap = unit(1, "mm"),
        border = TRUE,
        heatmap_legend_param = list(at = c(-1.5, 0, 1.5),
                                    labels = c("del", "", "amp"))) |>
  draw(column_title = "Chromosomal positions")

score_df <- data.frame(type = cell_type, score = cnv_score)
p_w <- wilcox.test(score ~ type, data = score_df)$p.value

ggplot(score_df, aes(type, score, fill = type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.55) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Malignant = "#B2182B", `Non-malignant` = "#4D4D4D")) +
  labs(title = sprintf("CNV score (Wilcoxon %s)",
       ifelse(p_w < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p_w))),
       x = NULL, y = "CNV score", fill = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

set.seed(43507)

## Three clones of one sample with a shared and two clone-specific events.
blocks <- data.frame(
  clone = c("clone A", "clone B", "clone C"),
  start = c(20, 20, 20),
  end   = c(90, 55, 90),
  cn    = c(2, 3, 1)
)

bins <- expand.grid(clone = c("clone A", "clone B", "clone C"),
                    pos = seq(10, 150, by = 1),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(cn = {
    hit <- blocks$cn[blocks$clone == clone & pos >= blocks$start &
                       pos < blocks$end]
    if (length(hit) == 0) 2 else hit[1]
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    log2r = log2(cn / 2) + rnorm(n(), 0, 0.07),
    ## BAF: at 2 copies heterozygotes sit at 0.5; at 3 copies the two allele
    ## bands split to 1/3 and 2/3; at 1 copy they collapse to 0 and 1.
    baf = case_when(
      cn == 2 ~ 0.5,
      cn == 3 ~ sample(c(1, 2) / 3, n(), replace = TRUE),
      cn == 1 ~ sample(c(0, 1), n(), replace = TRUE)
    ) + rnorm(n(), 0, 0.012)
  )

## Segments: one line per constant-copy-number run.
seg_lines <- bins |>
  group_by(clone) |>
  arrange(pos, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(cn_prev = lag(cn)) |>
  filter(is.na(cn_prev) | cn != cn_prev) |>
  mutate(xend = lead(pos, default = max(bins$pos) + 1),
         y = log2(cn / 2)) |>
  ungroup()

## The expected BAF bands for the two aberrant clones; drawn as expectations,
## not as a model fit, so the panel states what "should" happen.
baf_expect <- data.frame(
  clone = factor(rep(c("clone B", "clone C"), each = 2),
                 levels = c("clone A", "clone B", "clone C")),
  y = c(2 / 3, 1 / 3, 1, 0),
  x = c(20, 20, 20, 20),
  xend = c(55, 55, 90, 90)
)

p_depth <- ggplot(bins, aes(pos, log2r)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#7f7f7f", size = 0.22, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_segment(data = seg_lines, aes(x = pos, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y),
               colour = "#b2182b", linewidth = 0.55) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#525252", linewidth = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ clone, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = log2(c(1, 2, 3) / 2), labels = c("1", "2", "3"),
                     limits = c(-1.3, 0.9),
                     name = "copy number\n(ticks placed on the log2-ratio scale)") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 7.6, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(4, 5, 0, 5))

p_baf <- ggplot(bins, aes(pos, baf)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#7f7f7f", size = 0.22, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "#525252", linewidth = 0.25,
             linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_segment(data = baf_expect, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y),
               linetype = "22", colour = "#2166ac", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ clone, ncol = 1) +
  ## Keep the LOH extremes (BAF exactly 0/1) inside the panel: a hard
  ## c(0, 1) limit silently censors 37 bin points at or beyond the bounds.
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.04, 1.04), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(0, 150, 30)) +
  labs(x = "chromosome 1 position (Mb)", y = "B-allele frequency") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 7.6, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 5, 4, 5))

p_depth / p_baf + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.75))

set.seed(4358)

chroms <- tibble(
  chr = c("chr1", "chr2", "chr3"),
  len = c(248.96, 242.19, 198.30)   # Mb, GRCh38
)

## Two breakends per SV. 'dir' is the breakend orientation (+/-), which is what
## distinguishes an inversion from a duplication with the same endpoints.
sv <- tribble(
  ~id, ~type, ~chr1, ~pos1, ~dir1, ~chr2, ~pos2, ~dir2, ~copies,
  "SV01", "deletion",       "chr1", 62.4,  "+", "chr1", 64.1, "-", 1,
  "SV02", "tandem dup",     "chr1", 118.2, "-", "chr1", 119.0, "+", 3,
  "SV03", "inversion",      "chr2", 41.6,  "+", "chr2", 58.9, "+", 2,
  "SV04", "translocation",  "chr2", 170.3, "+", "chr3", 52.7, "-", 2,
  "SV05", "inversion",      "chr3", 8.4,   "+", "chr3", 61.2, "+", 2,
  "SV06", "fold-back inv",  "chr2", 205.6, "-", "chr2", 205.68, "-", 4
)

## Read evidence: split reads and discordant pairs per variant, sampled with
## a realistic skew (well-supported deletions, weak fold-backs).
evidence <- sv |>
  transmute(id, type,
            split = c(38, 24, 31, 19, 12, 6),
            discordant = c(61, 47, 52, 44, 22, 11))

carriers <- expand.grid(sample = sprintf("T%02d", 1:12), id = sv$id,
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  left_join(sv |> select(id, type), by = "id") |>
  mutate(p = case_when(
    type %in% c("deletion", "translocation") ~ 0.55,
    type %in% c("tandem dup", "inversion") ~ 0.35,
    TRUE ~ 0.18
  )) |>
  mutate(carried = runif(n()) < p) |>
  select(-p)

evidence |> rowwise() |> mutate(total = split + discordant) |> ungroup()

type_cols <- c("deletion" = "#2166ac", "tandem dup" = "#1b7837",
               "inversion" = "#d95f02", "translocation" = "#b2182b",
               "fold-back inv" = "#8c510a")

chr_y <- c(chr1 = 3, chr2 = 2, chr3 = 1)

arc_points <- function(x0, x1, y0, y1, n = 60, height = 0.55) {
  t <- seq(0, pi, length.out = n)
  data.frame(x = x0 + (x1 - x0) * (1 - cos(t)) / 2,
             y = y0 + (y1 - y0) * (1 - cos(t)) / 2 + height * sin(t))
}

arcs <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(sv)), function(i) {
  s <- sv[i, ]
  # A translocation is drawn as a wider, flatter arc between chromosome tracks.
  h <- if (s$type == "translocation") 0.30 else 0.55
  arc_points(s$pos1, s$pos2 + if (s$chr1 == s$chr2) 0 else 0,
             chr_y[[s$chr1]], chr_y[[s$chr2]], height = h) |>
    mutate(id = s$id, type = s$type)
}))

p_arc <- ggplot() +
  ## Chromosome tracks, lengths to scale on a shared Mb axis.
  geom_segment(data = chroms, aes(x = 0, xend = len, y = chr_y[chr],
                                  yend = chr_y[chr]),
               linewidth = 1.6, colour = "#d9d9d9", lineend = "round") +
  geom_text(data = chroms, aes(x = -4, y = chr_y[chr], label = chr),
            hjust = 1, size = 3, fontface = "bold", colour = "#333333") +
  geom_text(data = chroms, aes(x = len + 3, y = chr_y[chr],
                               label = paste0(len, " Mb")),
            hjust = 0, size = 2.4, colour = "#777777") +
  ## Arcs.
  geom_path(data = arcs, aes(x, y, group = id, colour = type,
                             linetype = type), linewidth = 0.55) +
  ## Breakend direction: a 6 Mb arrowhead on the chromosome bar pointing in
  ## the dir1/dir2 direction, so orientation is drawn, not implied.
  geom_segment(data = sv |> pivot_longer(c(pos1, pos2), names_to = "endn",
                                         values_to = "pos") |>
                 mutate(chr = if_else(endn == "pos1", chr1, chr2),
                        dir = if_else(endn == "pos1", dir1, dir2)),
               aes(x = pos, xend = pos + 6 * if_else(dir == "+", 1, -1),
                   y = chr_y[chr], yend = chr_y[chr]),
               arrow = arrow(ends = "last", length = unit(1.8, "mm")),
               linewidth = 0.55, colour = "#333333") +
  ## Copy-number consequence: a bar under each breakend pair whose thickness
  ## scales with the predicted copy number.
  geom_segment(data = filter(sv, chr1 == chr2),
               aes(x = pos1, xend = pos2, y = chr_y[chr1] - 0.16,
                   yend = chr_y[chr1] - 0.16, colour = type, linewidth = copies),
               show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_linewidth_continuous(range = c(0.5, 2.4), guide = "none") +
  ## Labels at the arc apex.
  geom_text_repel(data = arcs |> group_by(id, type) |>
                    slice_max(y, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup(),
                  aes(x, y, label = id, colour = type), size = 2.4,
                  nudge_y = 0.16, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0,
                  segment.size = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = type_cols, name = "SV type") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("deletion" = "solid", "tandem dup" = "solid",
                                   "inversion" = "dashed",
                                   "translocation" = "solid",
                                   "fold-back inv" = "dotted"),
                        name = "SV type") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-12, 265), breaks = seq(0, 250, 50),
                     labels = label_number(suffix = "")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.35, 4.3)) +
  labs(x = "Position (Mb, GRCh38)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7.6),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.34, "cm"))

p_arc

  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),

        legend.key.size = unit(0.32, "cm"))

p_car <- carriers |>

  geom_tile(aes(fill = carried), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3,

                .18, .14, .02, 0,  .09, .07, .01, 0), ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE)

         ref = site_ref[si], alt = site_alt[si],
         alt_frac = vaf[cbind(si, k)],
         frac = if_else(as.character(base) == ref, 1 - alt_frac - 3 * 0.0025,
                        if_else(as.character(base) == alt, alt_frac, 0.0025)),
         base = factor(base, levels = rev(bases))) |>

  G2 = data.frame(block = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "D", "F", "H", "G", "I", "J"),
                  orientation = c(rep("+", 6), "+", "-", "+", "+"),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  G3 = data.frame(block = c("A", "C", "D", "E", "F", "X", "H", "I", "J"),
                  orientation = rep("+", 9),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
)
block_len["X"] <- 0.9

## Cumulative block coordinates per genome, with a 0.2 Mb gap between blocks so
## adjacent blocks never read as one feature.
orders <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(genomes), function(g) {
  d <- genomes[[g]]
  d$len <- unname(block_len[d$block])
  d$start <- cumsum(c(0, head(d$len + 0.2, -1)))
  d$end <- d$start + d$len
  d$genome <- g
  d
}))

## Ribbon edges between consecutive genomes: one quadrilateral per shared
## block, from genome i to genome i+1.
ribbon <- function(from, to, y0, y1, n = 40) {
  s <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(intersect(from$block, to$block), function(b) {
    f <- from[from$block == b, ]
    t <- to[to$block == b, ]
    data.frame(block = b,
               x = c(f$start + s * (f$end - f$start),
                     rev(t$start + s * (t$end - t$start))),
               y = c(rep(y0, n), rep(y1, n)))
  }))
}
## One polygon per (block, genome pair). Grouping by block alone would stack
## the G1-G2 and G2-G3 quads of the same block into one self-intersecting
## polygon whose closing edge cuts back across the plot.
add_pair <- function(df, pair) { df$pair <- pair; df }

## PAD_KB is blank space between the drawn blocks on the ring. It is layout,
## not sequence, so it is kept out of the length that the ring label reports.
PAD_KB = 180

RING_R = [1.00, 0.86, 0.72]          # radius, outermost = reference
RING_W = 0.052                        # ring band thickness
GAP_DEG = 5.0                         # gap at 12 o'clock (start/end marker)
BLOCK_GAP = 0.9                       # degrees between adjacent blocks

def ring_angle(frac):
    """Map a 0..1 position along a ring to degrees, running clockwise."""
    return 90 - GAP_DEG / 2 - frac * (360 - GAP_DEG)

def xy(r, deg):
    t = np.deg2rad(deg)
    return np.array([r * np.cos(t), r * np.sin(t)])

def block_fractions(gi, bi):
    lens = block_len * shared[gi]
    cum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(lens)])
    pad = 90.0
    return ((pad + cum[bi]) / genome_len[gi],
            (pad + cum[bi + 1]) / genome_len[gi])

## ---- ring bands, split per block so presence is visible ----------------
for gi, radius in enumerate(RING_R):
    for bi in range(10):
        f0, f1 = block_fractions(gi, bi)
        d0, d1 = ring_angle(f0), ring_angle(f1)
        theta = np.linspace(np.deg2rad(d0 - BLOCK_GAP / 2),
                            np.deg2rad(d1 + BLOCK_GAP / 2), 60)
        if shared[gi, bi]:
            colour, lw, style = block_colours[gi], RING_W * 72, "-"
        else:
            colour, lw, style = "#e6e6e6", RING_W * 30, "-"
        ax.plot(np.cos(theta) * radius, np.sin(theta) * radius,
                color=colour, lw=lw, solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=3)
        if shared[gi, bi] and orientation[gi, bi] < 0:
            ## Inverted blocks get a white core: the ring is always split by
            ## presence first (colour) and by orientation second (fill).
            inner = radius
            ax.plot(np.cos(theta) * inner, np.sin(theta) * inner,
                    color="white", lw=RING_W * 26, solid_capstyle="butt",
                    zorder=4)
    ## Ring label outside the whole circle: the leader runs radially out
    ## through the outer rings so every label sits in clear white space.

    name = GENOMES[gi]

        a = xy(radius + RING_W / 2, deg)

        ax.plot([a[0], b[0]], [a[1], b[1]], color="#7a7a7a", lw=0.5, zorder=4)

## ---- ribbons from the reference block to each comparison block --------
def ribbon(gi, bi):
    s0, s1 = block_fractions(0, bi)
    t0, t1 = block_fractions(gi, bi)
    if orientation[gi, bi] < 0:
        t0, t1 = t1, t0
    n = 30
    src = [xy(RING_R[0] - RING_W / 2, ring_angle(f)) for f in np.linspace(s0, s1, n)]
    dst = [xy(RING_R[gi] - RING_W / 2, ring_angle(f)) for f in np.linspace(t0, t1, n)]
    return src + dst[::-1]

GENOMES = ["E. coli K-12", "E. coli O157:H7", "E. coli ST131"]
RING_R = [1.00, 0.86, 0.72]          # radius, outermost = reference
RING_W = 0.052                        # ring band thickness
GAP_DEG = 5.0                         # gap at 12 o'clock (start/end marker)
BLOCK_GAP = 0.9                       # degrees between adjacent blocks

def ring_angle(frac):
    """Map a 0..1 position along a ring to degrees, running clockwise."""
    return 90 - GAP_DEG / 2 - frac * (360 - GAP_DEG)

def xy(r, deg):
    t = np.deg2rad(deg)
    return np.array([r * np.cos(t), r * np.sin(t)])

def block_fractions(gi, bi):
    lens = block_len * shared[gi]
    cum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(lens)])
    pad = 90.0
    return ((pad + cum[bi]) / genome_len[gi],
            (pad + cum[bi + 1]) / genome_len[gi])

## ---- ribbons from the reference block to each comparison block --------
def ribbon(gi, bi):
    s0, s1 = block_fractions(0, bi)
    t0, t1 = block_fractions(gi, bi)
    if orientation[gi, bi] < 0:
        t0, t1 = t1, t0
    n = 30
    src = [xy(RING_R[0] - RING_W / 2, ring_angle(f)) for f in np.linspace(s0, s1, n)]
    dst = [xy(RING_R[gi] - RING_W / 2, ring_angle(f)) for f in np.linspace(t0, t1, n)]
    return src + dst[::-1]

def gaussian_sum(centres, heights, widths):
    out = np.zeros_like(rel, dtype=float)
    for c, h, w in zip(centres, heights, widths):
        out += h * np.exp(-0.5 * ((rel - c) / w) ** 2)
    return out

## Cluster prevalence: a realistic U-shaped pangenome curve, with a small
## core plateau rather than a clean power law.
prevalence = np.clip(
    (np.random.beta(0.45, 2.6, n_clusters) * n_genomes).astype(int), 1, n_genomes
)
prevalence[np.random.choice(n_clusters, 180, replace=False)] = n_genomes

cluster_class = np.where(prevalence == n_genomes, "core",
                 np.where(prevalence == 1, "unique", "accessory"))

## Presence matrix. Core clusters are present everywhere. Accessory clusters
## are mostly clade-specific mobile elements: each is anchored in one of five
## clades, with a small rate of horizontal transfer into other strains. That
## mixture is what makes a phylogenetically ordered matrix show blocks.
clade_of_genome = np.repeat(np.arange(5), 4)          # 5 clades x 4 strains
clade_order = np.concatenate([np.arange(c * 4, c * 4 + 4) for c in range(5)])
present = np.zeros((n_genomes, n_clusters), dtype=bool)
for j in range(n_clusters):
    if prevalence[j] == n_genomes:
        present[:, j] = True
        continue
    anchor_clade = np.random.randint(5)
    clade_members = np.where(clade_of_genome == anchor_clade)[0]
    foreign = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(n_genomes), clade_members)
    ## Start from the anchored clade, then add sporadic carriers elsewhere.
    carriers = set(np.random.choice(clade_members,
                                    size=min(len(clade_members), prevalence[j]),
                                    replace=False).tolist())
    while len(carriers) < prevalence[j]:
        carriers.add(int(np.random.choice(foreign)))
    present[sorted(carriers), j] = True

  library(ggplot2)

set.seed(43512)

## A 100 Mb chromosome at 500 kb resolution with five TADs. Contacts are drawn
## as a sparse (i, j, count) table, which is what Hi-C pipelines emit.
res <- 0.5
n_bin <- 200
tad_edges <- c(0, 22, 45, 55, 90, 100)
tad_id <- cut(seq_len(n_bin) * res - res / 2, breaks = tad_edges,
              labels = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE)

contacts <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(n_bin), j = seq_len(n_bin)) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(i >= j) |>                       # x = i, y = j -> keep x >= y
  mutate(
    d = (i - j) * res,
    decay = 1 / (1 + d),                  # P(s) ~ s^-1
    same_tad = tad_id[i] == tad_id[j],
    freq = decay * ifelse(same_tad, 3.2, 0.9) * rexp(n(), 1)
  )

## Observed/expected: divide by the mean count at each contact distance.
oe <- contacts |>
  mutate(d_bin = round(d / res)) |>
  group_by(d_bin) |>
  mutate(mean_d = mean(freq)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ## The observed/expected ratio is kept at bin resolution (no distance-band
  ## smoothing); the per-distance expectation removes the s^-1 decay without
  ## touching the TAD-to-TAD contrast.
  mutate(oe = log2((freq + 0.05) / (mean_d + 0.05)),
         x = i * res, y = j * res)

bounds <- data.frame(x = tad_edges[-c(1, length(tad_edges))])
pal <- c("#313695", "#4575b4", "#abd9e9", "#ffffbf", "#fdae61", "#d73027",
         "#a50026")

p_tri <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = oe, aes(x, y, fill = oe),
              interpolate = FALSE) +
  ## A boundary b is a single point (b, b) on the diagonal, so inside the data
  ## region x >= y it can only be drawn as two segments from that point:
  ## x = b with 0 <= y <= b, and y = b with b <= x <= 100. Full rules would
  ## advertise contacts the matrix does not contain.
  geom_segment(data = bounds,
               aes(x = x, xend = x, y = 0, yend = x),
               colour = "grey10", linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "22") +
  geom_segment(data = bounds,
               aes(x = x, xend = 100, y = x, yend = x),
               colour = "grey10", linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "22") +
  scale_fill_gradientn("log2\nobs/exp", colours = pal, limits = c(-2.2, 2.2),
                       oob = scales::squish) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
  ## scale_y_reverse() is what actually flips the axis: bin 0 at the top-left,
  ## the diagonal from top-left to bottom-right, and the data triangle filling
  ## the upper-right half -- the layout used by Hi-C browsers.
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "position (Mb)", y = "position (Mb)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.key.height = unit(0.85, "cm"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.8),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 7.2))

## Shear ("rotation"): u = genomic midpoint, v = contact separation.
rot <- oe |> mutate(u = (i + j) * res / 2, v = (i - j) * res)

p_rot <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = rot, aes(u, v, fill = oe), interpolate = FALSE) +
  ## The (u, v) transform is a 2:1 shear, not a 45-degree rotation: a boundary
  ## b is an apex at (b, 0) and its flanks are the lines v = +/- 2 (u - b),
  ## i.e. slope +/- 2 through the apex. Slope +/- 1 guides would cut across
  ## the TAD triangles instead of tracing their edges.
  geom_abline(data = transform(bounds, s = +2, i = -2 * x),
              aes(slope = s, intercept = i), colour = "grey10",
              linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "22") +
  geom_abline(data = transform(bounds, s = -2, i = 2 * x),
              aes(slope = s, intercept = i), colour = "grey10",
              linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "22") +
  scale_fill_gradientn("log2\nobs/exp", colours = pal, limits = c(-2.2, 2.2),
                       oob = scales::squish, guide = "none") +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)) +
  labs(x = "genomic midpoint (Mb)", y = "separation (Mb)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6.8))

p_tri + p_rot + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1))

## 16 samples x 30 PCs of malignant-cell embeddings (Seurat PCA surrogate):
## planted per-sample dispersion -> two heterogeneity groups
samples <- sprintf("P%02d", 1:16)
n_cells <- c(110, 95, 130, 85, 120, 100, 90, 105, 115, 88, 125, 92, 108, 96, 84, 112)
disp <- c(1.4, 1.1, 2.6, 0.9, 2.2, 1.0, 1.2, 2.4,
          1.3, 0.8, 2.5, 1.0, 1.1, 0.9, 1.2, 2.3)  # 6 heterogeneous samples
emb <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(samples), function(i) {
  m <- matrix(rnorm(n_cells[i] * 30, 0, disp[i]), n_cells[i], 30)
  m[, 1] <- m[, 1] + i * 0.4          # sample separation on PC1
  data.frame(m, Sample = samples[i])
}))
## the algorithm as described in the paper: distance to the sample centroid
## in PC space, with 2-SD outlier removal on the top 3 PCs
calcDiversityScore <- function(eigenvectorSpace, inWhichTumor,
                               removeOutiler = TRUE, nsd = 2, topPCs = 1:3) {
  centroidMean <- apply(eigenvectorSpace, 2, function(x) tapply(x, inWhichTumor, mean))
  centroidMeanExpand <- centroidMean[match(inWhichTumor, rownames(centroidMean)), ]
  if (removeOutiler) {
    centroidSD <- apply(eigenvectorSpace, 2, function(x) tapply(x, inWhichTumor, sd))
    centroidSDExpand <- centroidSD[match(inWhichTumor, rownames(centroidSD)), ]
    outlierMatrix <- (eigenvectorSpace < centroidMeanExpand - nsd * centroidSDExpand) |
      (eigenvectorSpace > centroidMeanExpand + nsd * centroidSDExpand)
    outlierInd <- apply(outlierMatrix[, topPCs], 1, all)
    centroidMeanExpand <- centroidMeanExpand[!outlierInd, ]
    eigenvectorSpace <- eigenvectorSpace[!outlierInd, ]
    inWhichTumor <- inWhichTumor[!outlierInd]
    message(sum(outlierInd), " outlier cells were removed")
  }
  tapply(sqrt(rowSums((eigenvectorSpace - centroidMeanExpand)^2)), inWhichTumor, mean)
}
mat <- as.matrix(emb[, grep("^X", names(emb), value = TRUE)])
colnames(mat) <- paste0("PC", 1:30)
div <- calcDiversityScore(mat, emb$Sample)

gg <- data.frame(score = as.numeric(div),
                 Group = factor(ifelse(div > med, "Div-High", "Div-Low"), c("Div-Low", "Div-High")),
                 ID = names(div))
se <- function(x) sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
summ <- aggregate(score ~ Group, gg, function(v) c(mean = mean(v), se = se(v)))

  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 9, shape = 95, show.legend = FALSE) +

clust <- c("OO", "GC", "SC", "EC")
genes7 <- c("DDX4", "AMH", "COL1A2", "CDH5")
rows <- list()
for (cl in seq_along(clust)) {
  for (gn in seq_along(genes7)) {
    for (ag in seq_along(c("Y", "O"))) {
      base <- rnorm(24, mean = 2.2 + 0.4 * cl + 0.3 * gn, sd = 0.9)
      # marker gene: one cluster expresses high; old shifts up on the top marker
      if (gn == cl) base <- base + 2.3
      if (gn == 1 && cl == 1 && ag == 2) base <- base + 1.9
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        aging = c("Y", "O")[ag], cluster_short = clust[cl], gene = genes7[gn],
        expression = base, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}

dfc$aging <- factor(dfc$aging, levels = c("Y", "O"))
dfc$cluster_short <- factor(dfc$cluster_short, levels = clust)
dfc$gene <- factor(dfc$gene, levels = genes7)
# gate: the DDX4/OO facet is significantly higher in Old (the designed effect)
sub <- dfc[dfc$gene == "DDX4" & dfc$cluster_short == "OO", ]
wt <- wilcox.test(expression ~ aging, data = sub)

set.seed(20201)
## 40 genes: 20 glycolytic + 20 cholesterogenic, 80 samples (tumours as features)
n_gly <- 20; n_chol <- 20; n_sam <- 80
gly <- sprintf("GLY%02d", 1:n_gly); chol <- sprintf("CHO%02d", 1:n_chol)
expr <- matrix(rnorm((n_gly + n_chol) * n_sam), n_gly + n_chol, n_sam,
               dimnames = list(c(gly, chol), sprintf("T%02d", 1:n_sam)))
## planted co-expression: gly genes follow pattern A, chol pattern B
patA <- sin(seq(0, 3 * pi, length.out = n_sam)) + rnorm(n_sam, 0, 0.4)
patB <- cos(seq(0, 3 * pi, length.out = n_sam)) + rnorm(n_sam, 0, 0.4)
expr[1:n_gly, ] <- expr[1:n_gly, ] + patA * 1.2
expr[(n_gly + 1):(n_gly + n_chol), ] <- expr[(n_gly + 1):(n_gly + n_chol), ] + patB * 1.2
genes_obs <- t(scale(t(expr)))          # genes as observations, samples as features
## minimal consensus clustering: resample observations, cluster, accumulate
## the co-clustering frequency (what ConsensusClusterPlus does internally)
reps <- 100; k <- 3
n_obs <- nrow(genes_obs)
co <- matrix(0, n_obs, n_obs, dimnames = list(rownames(genes_obs), rownames(genes_obs)))
set.seed(2020103)
for (r in seq_len(reps)) {
  idx <- sample(n_obs, round(0.8 * n_obs), TRUE)
  hc <- hclust(dist(genes_obs[idx, ]), method = "ward.D2")
  cl <- cutree(hc, k = k)
  for (a in seq_along(idx)) for (b in seq_along(idx)) {
    if (a != b && cl[a] == cl[b]) co[idx[a], idx[b]] <- co[idx[a], idx[b]] + 1
  }
}
co <- co / reps
final <- hclust(as.dist(1 - co), method = "ward.D2")
cl <- cutree(final, k = k)
gene_cluster <- paste0("C", cl)

ann_col <- data.frame(Cluster = paste0("C", cl), row.names = rownames(co))
ann_col$Pathway <- c(rep("Glycolytic", n_gly), rep("Cholesterogenic", n_chol))[rownames(ann_col)]
ann_colors <- list(Cluster = c(C1 = "#7B9C4A", C2 = "#7F1D47", C3 = "#BDA597"),
                   Pathway = c(Glycolytic = "black", Cholesterogenic = "#A7DCF8"))
pheatmap(co[order(cl), order(cl)],
         color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "#3A236B"))(64),
         cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
         annotation_col = ann_col, annotation_colors = ann_colors,
         show_rownames = FALSE, show_colnames = FALSE,
         border_color = NA, legend = TRUE,
         cellwidth = 10, cellheight = 9, # fixed cell size: keeps the legend labels inside the canvas
         main = "Consensus matrix, k = 3 (gene dimension, simulated)")

## cohort matrices: immune-cell scores from planted module factors
## (cytotoxic / APC / myeloid; Tregs anti-correlate with cytotoxicity)
mk <- function(seed, n, module_scale = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  f_cyt <- rnorm(n); f_apc <- rnorm(n); f_mye <- rnorm(n)
  base <- cbind(
    aDC = f_apc + rnorm(n, 0, 0.7), `B cells` = rnorm(n),
    `CD8 T cells` = f_cyt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.6),
    `Cytotoxic lymphocytes` = f_cyt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.6),
    DC = f_apc + rnorm(n, 0, 0.8), Eosinophils = rnorm(n),
    Macrophages = f_mye + rnorm(n, 0, 0.7), `Mast cells` = rnorm(n),
    Neutrophils = f_mye + rnorm(n, 0, 0.9), `NK cells` = f_cyt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.8),
    pDC = f_apc + rnorm(n, 0, 1.0), `T cells` = f_cyt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.7),
    `T helper cells` = f_cyt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.8),
    `T regulatory cells` = module_scale * (-f_cyt) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.9))
  base <- base * module_scale + rnorm(n * length(cells), 0, 0.3)
  colnames(base) <- cells
  R <- P <- matrix(0, length(cells), length(cells), dimnames = list(cells, cells))
  for (i in seq_along(cells)) for (j in seq_along(cells)) {
    ct <- cor.test(base[, i], base[, j])
    R[i, j] <- ct$estimate; P[i, j] <- ct$p.value
  }
  list(R = R, P = P)
}
